umbrella review.text: In medical research, an umbrella review is a review of systematic reviews or meta-analyses.

sleep quality.text: Sleep is a state of reduced mental and physical activity in which consciousness is altered and certain sensory activity is inhibited.

mixture-of-experts.text: Mixture of experts (MoE) is a machine learning technique where multiple expert networks (learners) are used to divide a problem space into homogeneous regions.

feasibility study.text: A feasibility study is an assessment of the practicality of a project or system.

ambient intelligence.text: Ambient intelligence (AmI) refers to environments with electronic devices that are aware of and can recognize the presence of human beings and adapt accordingly.

human-robot interaction.text: Human–robot interaction (HRI) is the study of interactions between humans and robots.

data minimisation.text: Data minimization is the principle of collecting, processing and storing only the necessary amount of personal information required for a specific purpose.

structural equation modeling.text: Structural equation modeling (SEM) is a diverse set of methods used by scientists for both observational and experimental research.

dental implants.text: A dental implant is a prosthesis that interfaces with the bone of the jaw or skull to support a dental prosthesis such as a crown, bridge, denture, or facial prosthesis or to act as an orthodontic anchor.

prostate cancer.text: Prostate cancer is the uncontrolled growth of cells in the prostate, a gland in the male reproductive system below the bladder.

mri scan.text: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a medical imaging technique used in radiology to generate pictures of the anatomy and the physiological processes inside the body.

real-world evidence.text: Real-world evidence (RWE) in medicine is the clinical evidence regarding the usage and potential benefits or risks of a medical product derived from analysis of real-world data (RWD).

community resilience.text: Community resilience is the sustained ability of a community to use available resources to respond to, withstand, and recover from adverse situations.

plasmids.text: A plasmid is a small, extrachromosomal DNA molecule within a cell that is physically separated from chromosomal DNA and can replicate independently.

hpv.text: Human papillomavirus infection is an infection caused by a DNA virus from the Papillomaviridae family.

cervical cancer.text: Cervical cancer is a type of cancer that develops in the cervix, the lower narrow part of the uterus (womb).

coastal erosion.text: Coastal erosion is the loss or displacement of land, or the long-term removal of sediment and rocks along the coastline due to the action of waves, currents, tides, wind-driven water, waterborne ice, or other impacts of storms.

fmri.text: Functional magnetic resonance imaging or functional MRI (fMRI) measures brain activity by detecting changes associated with blood flow.

semantic roles.text: In certain theories of linguistics, thematic relations, also known as semantic roles or thematic roles, are the various roles that a noun phrase may play with respect to the action or state described by a governing verb, commonly the sentence's main verb.

xenophobia.text: Xenophobia is the fear or dislike of people who are perceived as being foreign or strange.

autoimmune conditions.text: An autoimmune disease is a condition causing disease that results from an anomalous response of the adaptive immune system, wherein it mistakenly targets and attacks healthy, functioning parts of the body as if they were foreign organisms.

menstrual cycle.text: The menstrual cycle is a series of natural changes in hormone production and the structures of the uterus and ovaries of the female reproductive system that makes pregnancy possible.

net present value.text: Net present value (NPV), also known as net present worth (NPW) is a method for assessing whether future amounts of money are worth more or less than the cost of an investment made today.

named storm.text: Tropical cyclones and subtropical cyclones are named by various warning centers to simplify communication between forecasters and the general public regarding forecasts, watches and warnings.

weather warnings.text: At sea, a storm warning is a warning issued by the National Weather Service of the United States when winds between 48 and 63 knots are occurring or predicted to occur soon.

gestational diabetes.text: Gestational diabetes is a condition in which an individual without diabetes develops high blood sugar levels during pregnancy.

androgenetic alopecia.text: Pattern hair loss, also known as androgenetic alopecia, is a hair loss condition that primarily affects the top and front of the scalp.

ai-generated video.text: A text-to-video model is a form of generative AI that uses a natural language description as input to produce a video relevant to the input text.

psychological resilience.text: Psychological resilience, or mental resilience, is the ability to cope mentally and emotionally with a crisis, or to return to pre-crisis status quickly.

cognitive load.text: In cognitive psychology, cognitive load is the effort being used in the working memory.

solid tumors.text: A neoplasm is a type of abnormal and excessive growth of cells.

tegoprubart.text: Tegoprubart (AT-1501) is an experimental humanized monoclonal antibody that inhibits CD40L.

tacrolimus.text: Tacrolimus, sold under the brand name Prograf among others, is an immunosuppressive drug.

bacteriophages.text: A bacteriophage, also known informally as a phage, is a virus that infects and replicates within bacteria.

quality of life.text: Quality of life (QOL) is defined by the World Health Organization as "an individual's perception of their position in life in the context of the culture and value systems in which they live and in relation to their goals, expectations, standards and concerns".

coral reefs.text: A coral reef is an underwater ecosystem characterized by reef-building corals.

sensory perception.text: Perception is the identification, interpretation and organization of sensory information, in order to represent and understand the presented information or environment.

myasthenia gravis.text: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is a long-term neuromuscular junction disease that leads to varying degrees of skeletal muscle weakness.

monetary policy.text: Monetary policy is the policy adopted by the monetary authority of a nation to affect monetary and other financial conditions to accomplish broader objectives like high employment and price stability.

arbitrageurs.text: Betting arbitrage is an example of arbitrage arising on betting markets due to either bookmakers' differing opinions on event outcomes, or errors.

dinosaur.text: Dinosaurs are a diverse group of warmblooded reptiles of the clade Dinosauria.

flowering plants.text: Flowering plants are plants that bear flowers and fruits, and form the clade Angiospermae or Magnoliophyta.

parrot.text: Parrots, also known as psittacines from the name of the type genus Psittacus, are birds with a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet.

water security.text: The aim of water security is to maximize the benefits of water for humans and ecosystems.

water governance.text: Environmental governance are the processes of decision-making involved in the control and management of the environment and natural resources.

parenting.text: Parenting or child rearing promotes and supports the physical, cognitive, social, emotional, and educational development from infancy to adulthood.

deepfake.text: Deepfakes are images, videos, or audio that have been edited or generated using artificial intelligence, AI-based tools or audio-video editing software.

image-based sexual abuse.text: Revenge porn is the distribution of sexually explicit images or videos of individuals without their consent, with the punitive intention to create public humiliation or character assassination out of revenge against the victim.

theory of mind.text: In psychology and philosophy, theory of mind is the capacity to understand other individuals by ascribing mental states to them.

social cognition.text: Social cognition is a topic within psychology that focuses on how people process, store, and apply information about other people and social situations.

reading comprehension.text: Reading comprehension is the ability to process written text, understand its meaning, and to integrate with what the reader already knows.

conversational ai.text: A chatbot is a software application or web interface designed to converse through text or speech, functioning as a conversation partner.

primary care.text: Primary care is the day-to-day healthcare given by a health care provider.

bdnf.text: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (Bdnf), or abrineurin, is a protein that, in humans, is encoded by the BDNF gene.

overall survival.text: Survival rate is a part of survival analysis.

genetic diversity.text: Genetic diversity is the total number of genetic characteristics in the genetic makeup of a species.

differential diagnosis.text: In healthcare, a differential diagnosis (DDx) is a method of analysis that distinguishes a particular disease or condition from others that present with similar clinical features.

extreme weather.text: Extreme weather includes unexpected, unusual, severe, or unseasonal weather; weather at the extremes of the historical distribution—the range that has been seen in the past.

aquaporin-4.text: Aquaporin-4, also known as AQP-4, is a water channel protein encoded by the AQP4 gene in humans.

brain scanning.text: Neuroimaging is the use of quantitative (computational) techniques to study the structure and function of the central nervous system, developed as an objective way of scientifically studying the healthy human brain in a non-invasive manner.

integers.text: An integer is the number zero (0), a positive natural number, or the negation of a positive natural number.

fractions.text: A fraction represents a part of a whole or, more generally, any number of equal parts.

regenerated cellulose.text: Rayon, also called viscose, is a semi-synthetic fiber made from natural sources of regenerated cellulose, such as wood and related agricultural products.

principal components.text: Principal component analysis (PCA) is a linear dimensionality reduction technique with applications in exploratory data analysis, visualization and data preprocessing.

asset pricing.text: In financial economics, asset pricing refers to the formal development of the principles used in pricing, together with the resultant models.

heat wave.text: A heat wave or heatwave, sometimes described as extreme heat, is a period of abnormally hot weather that lasts for multiple days.

cancer treatment.text: Cancer treatments are a wide range of treatments available for the many different types of cancer, with each cancer type needing its own specific treatment.

effect size.text: In statistics, an effect size is a quantitative measure of the magnitude and often direction of a phenomenon.

cardiovascular health.text: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is any disease involving the heart or blood vessels.

tobacco use.text: Tobacco smoking is the practice of burning tobacco and the absorption of the resulting smoke into one's body.

mtor.text: The mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR), also known as mammalian target of rapamycin, is a serine-threonine protein kinase that regulates cell growth, cell proliferation, cell motility, cell survival, protein synthesis, autophagy, and transcription.

structural equation model.text: Structural equation modeling (SEM) is a diverse set of methods used by scientists for both observational and experimental research.

abuse of power.text: Abuse of power or abuse of authority, in the form of "malfeasance in office" or "official abuse of power", is the commission of an unlawful act, done in an official capacity, which affects the performance of official duties.

cancer survivors.text: A cancer survivor is a person with or beyond cancer of any type who is still living.

wearable technology.text: Wearable technology is devices that are worn on, near, or inside the human body.

hydrogen peroxide.text: Hydrogen peroxide is a chemical compound with the formula H2O2.

europe.text: Europe is a continent located entirely in the Northern Hemisphere and mostly in the Eastern Hemisphere.

creativity.text: Creativity is the ability to generate novel and valuable ideas or works through the exercise of imagination.

confidence.text: Confidence is the feeling of belief or trust that a person or thing is reliable.

variable selection.text: In machine learning, feature selection is the process of selecting a subset of relevant features for use in model construction.

planetary health.text: Planetary Health refers to the interdependence of human and environmental health.

retatrutide.text: Retatrutide is an experimental drug for obesity developed by the American pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly and Company.

multilateralism.text: In international relations, multilateralism refers to an alliance of multiple countries pursuing a common goal.

physical education.text: Physical education is an academic subject taught in schools worldwide, encompassing primary, secondary, and sometimes tertiary education.

personalization.text: Personalization consists of tailoring a service or product to accommodate specific individuals.

recommender systems.text: A recommender system, also called a recommendation engine or content discovery platform is a type of information filtering system that aims to suggest items most relevant for some input or to a particular user.

spatial reasoning.text: Spatial–temporal reasoning is an area of artificial intelligence that draws from the fields of computer science, cognitive science, and cognitive psychology.

reference frames.text: In physics and astronomy, a frame of reference is an abstract coordinate system, whose origin, orientation, and scale have been specified in physical space.

foreign aid.text: In international relations, aid is – from the perspective of governments – a voluntary transfer of resources from one country to another.

neuropsychiatric symptoms.text: Signs and symptoms (S/S) are diagnostic indications of an illness, injury, or condition.

default risk.text: Credit risk is the chance that a borrower does not repay a loan or fulfill a loan obligation.

subfamily.text: A subfamily is an auxiliary (intermediate) taxonomic rank, positioned below family and above genus.

climate.text: Climate is the long-term weather pattern in a region, typically averaged over 30 years.

sdgs.text: Sustainable Development Goals were adopted in 2015 by all United Nations (UN) members for the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

postprandial glucose.text: A postprandial glucose (PPG) test is a blood glucose test that determines the amount of glucose in the plasma after a meal.

expectancy-value theory.text: Expectancy–value theory has been developed in many different fields including education, health, communications, marketing and economics.

industrial unrest.text: A labour revolt or workers' uprising is a period of civil unrest characterised by strong labour militancy and strike activity.

tsunami.text: A tsunami is a series of waves in a water body caused by the displacement of a large volume of water, generally in an ocean or a large lake.

glacier retreat.text: The retreat of glaciers since 1850 is a well-documented effect of climate change.

foodborne pathogens.text: Food microbiology is the study of the microorganisms that inhabit, create, or contaminate food.

food safety.text: Food safety is a scientific method describing handling, preparation, and storage of food in a way or ways that prevent foodborne illness.

peer review.text: Peer review is the evaluation of work by one or more people with similar competencies as the producers of the work.

replanting.text: In agriculture and gardening, transplanting or replanting is the technique of moving a plant from one location to another.

academic performance.text: Academic achievement or academic performance is the extent to which a student, teacher or institution has attained their short or long-term educational goals.

delayed reward.text: Delayed gratification, or deferred gratification, is the ability to resist the temptation of an immediate reward in favor of a more valuable and long-lasting reward later.

disc1.text: Disrupted in schizophrenia 1 is a protein that in humans is encoded by the DISC1 gene.

prodromal.text: In medicine, a prodrome is an early sign or symptom that often indicates the onset of a disease before more diagnostically specific signs and symptoms develop.

risk perception.text: Risk perception is the subjective judgement that people make about the characteristics and severity of a risk.

academic dishonesty.text: Academic dishonesty, academic misconduct, academic fraud and academic integrity are related concepts that refer to various actions on the part of students that go against the expected norms of a school, university or other learning institution.

patient confidentiality.text: Physician–patient privilege is a legal concept, related to medical confidentiality, that protects communications between a patient and their doctor from being used against the patient in court.

intensive margin.text: Within economics, margin is a concept used to describe the current level of consumption or production of a goods or service.

alzheimer’s.text: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disease and is the most common cause of dementia, accounting for around 60–70% of cases.

standardized testing.text: A standardized test is a test that is administered and scored in a consistent or standard manner.

science fiction.text: Science fiction is the genre of speculative fiction that imagines advanced and futuristic changes in technology, scientific knowledge, or biological systems.

ehealth.text: eHealth describes healthcare services which are supported by digital processes, communication or technology such as electronic prescribing, Telehealth, or Electronic Health Records (EHRs).

social behaviour.text: Social behavior is behavior among two or more organisms within the same species, it encompasses any behavior in which one member affects another.

acclimatisation.text: Acclimatization or acclimatisation is the process in which an individual organism adjusts to a change in its environment, allowing it to maintain fitness across a range of environmental conditions.

attributable risk.text: The risk difference (RD), excess risk, or attributable risk is the difference between the risk of an outcome in the exposed group and the unexposed group.

actigraphy.text: Actigraphy is a non-invasive method of monitoring human rest/activity cycles.

preprint.text: In academic publishing, a preprint is a version of a scholarly or scientific paper that precedes formal peer review and publication in a peer-reviewed scholarly or scientific journal.

exercise therapy.text: Physical therapy (PT), also known as physiotherapy, is a healthcare profession, as well as the care provided by physical therapists.

cancer surgery.text: Surgical oncology is the branch of surgery applied to oncology; it focuses on the surgical management of tumors, especially cancerous tumors.

brief intervention.text: Brief intervention can often be referred to as screening and brief intervention (SBI) or, in England, identification and brief advice (IBA).

fetal alcohol spectrum disorders.text: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASDs) are a group of conditions that can occur in a person who is exposed to alcohol during gestation.

subjective experience.text: The subjective character of experience, also referred to as subjective experience, is the first-person aspect of conscious experience.

gastric cancer.text: Stomach cancer, also known as gastric cancer, is a malignant tumor of the stomach.

chronic inflammation.text: Inflammation is part of the biological defence response of body tissues.

red meat.text: In the context of nutrition, red meat is defined as meat obtained from mammals, including beef, pork, lamb/mutton, veal, and venison.

sea levels.text: Mean sea level is an average surface level of one or more among Earth's coastal bodies of water from which heights such as elevation may be measured.

coastal flooding.text: Coastal flooding occurs when dry and low-lying land is submerged (flooded) by seawater.

haze.text: Haze is traditionally an atmospheric phenomenon in which dust, smoke, and other dry particulates suspended in air obscure visibility and the clarity of the sky.

indonesia.text: Indonesia, officially the Republic of Indonesia, is a country in Southeast Asia and Oceania, between the Indian and Pacific oceans.

agricultural communication.text: Agricultural communication, or agricultural communications, is a field that focuses on communication about agriculture-related information among agricultural stakeholders and between agricultural and non-agricultural sta

sustainable intensification.text: Intensive agriculture, also known as intensive farming, conventional, or industrial agriculture, is a type of agriculture, both of crop plants and of animals, with higher levels of input and output per unit of agricultural land area.

excise tax.text: An excise, or excise tax, is any duty on a category of goods that is normally levied by a government at the moment of manufacture for domestic consumption.

price elasticity of demand.text: A good's price elasticity of demand is a measure of how sensitive the quantity demanded is to its price.

tax progressivity.text: A progressive tax is a tax in which the tax rate increases as the taxable amount increases.

metacognitive strategies.text: Metacognition is an awareness of one's thought processes and an understanding of the patterns behind them.

learning analytics.text: Learning analytics is the measurement, collection, analysis and reporting of data about learners and their contexts, for purposes of understanding and optimizing learning and the environments in which it occurs.

sexual dysfunction.text: Sexual dysfunction is difficulty experienced by an individual or partners during any stage of normal sexual activity, including physical pleasure, desire, preference, arousal, or orgasm.

influenza.text: Influenza, commonly known as the flu, is an infectious disease caused by influenza viruses.

population immunity.text: Herd immunity is a form of indirect protection that applies only to contagious diseases.

ezhip.text: EZH inhibitory protein is a protein that in humans is encoded by the gene EZHIP.

face perception.text: Facial perception is an individual's understanding and interpretation of the face.

zolpidem.text: Zolpidem, sold under the brand name Ambien among others, is a medication primarily used for the short-term treatment of sleeping problems.

behavioral economics.text: Behavioral economics is the study of the psychological factors involved in the decisions of individuals or institutions, and how these decisions deviate from those implied by traditional economic theory.

wheat cultivar.text: Wheat is a group of wild and domesticated grasses of the genus Triticum.

liver.text: The liver is a major metabolic organ exclusively found in vertebrates which performs many essential biological functions, such as detoxification of the organism and the synthesis of various proteins and other biochemicals necessary for digestion and growth.

metabolic dysfunction.text: Metabolic syndrome is a clustering of at least three of the following five medical conditions: abdominal obesity, high blood pressure, high blood sugar, high serum triglycerides, and low serum high-density lipoprotein (HDL).

vaping.text: An electronic cigarette (e-cigarette) or vape is a device that simulates tobacco smoking.

harm-reduction.text: Harm reduction, or harm minimization, refers to a range of intentional practices and public health policies designed to lessen the negative social and/or physical consequences associated with various human behaviors, both legal and illegal.

sweeteners.text: A sweetener is a substance added to food or drink to impart the flavor of sweetness, either because it contains a type of sugar, or because it contains a sweet-tasting sugar substitute.

palaeolithic.text: The Paleolithic, or Old Stone Age, is a period in human prehistory distinguished by the original development of stone tools.

rock art.text: In archaeology, rock art refers to human-made markings placed on natural surfaces, typically vertical stone surfaces.

marketing strategy.text: Marketing strategy refers to the set of coordinated actions undertaken by an organization to increase sales, strengthen market presence, and achieve sustainable competitive advantage.

swot analysis.text: In strategic planning and strategic management, SWOT analysis is a decision-making technique that identifies the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats of an organization or project.

loan officer.text: Loan officers evaluate, authorize, or recommend approval of loan applications for people and businesses.

learning management system.text: A Learning Management System (LMS) is a software application for the administration, documentation, tracking, reporting, automation, and delivery of educational courses, training programs, materials, or learning and development programs.

oral polio vaccine.text: Polio vaccine is a vaccine used to prevent poliomyelitis (polio).

essential tremor.text: Essential tremor (ET), also called benign tremor, familial tremor, and idiopathic tremor, is a medical condition characterized by involuntary rhythmic contractions and relaxations of certain muscle groups in one or more body parts of unknown cause.

thalamotomy.text: Thalamotomy is a surgical procedure in which a functional lesion is made into the thalamus to improve the overall brain function in patients.

lignin.text: Lignin is a class of complex organic polymers that form key structural materials in the support tissues of most plants.

enterolignans.text: The lignans are a large group of low molecular weight polyphenols found in plants, particularly seeds, whole grains, and vegetables.

indian ocean.text: The Indian Ocean is the third-largest of the world's five oceanic divisions, covering 70,560,000 km2 (27,240,000 sq mi) or approximately 20% of the water area of Earth's surface.

electroconvulsive therapy.text: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a psychiatric treatment that causes a generalized seizure by passing electrical current through the brain.

drake equation.text: The Drake equation is a probabilistic argument used to estimate the number of active, communicative extraterrestrial civilizations in the Milky Way Galaxy.

santa ana winds.text: The Santa Ana winds, occasionally referred to as the devil winds, are strong, extremely dry katabatic winds that originate inland and affect coastal Southern California and northern Baja California.

digital health.text: Digital health is a discipline that includes digital care programs, technologies with health, healthcare, living, and society to enhance the efficiency of healthcare delivery and to make medicine more personalized and precise.

cataract.text: A cataract is a cloudy area in the lens of the eye that impairs vision.

nitrogen dioxide.text: Nitrogen dioxide is a chemical compound with the formula NO2.

cognitive appraisal.text: Cognitive appraisal is the subjective interpretation made by an individual to stimuli in the environment.

social insurance.text: Social insurance is a form of social welfare that provides insurance against economic risks.

randomized trial.text: In science, randomized experiments are the experiments that allow the greatest reliability and validity of statistical estimates of treatment effects.

l-dopa.text: l-DOPA, also known as l-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine and used medically as levodopa, is made and used as part of the normal biology of some plants and animals, including humans.

genetic engineering.text: Genetic engineering, also called genetic modification or genetic manipulation, is the modification and manipulation of an organism's genes using technology.

synthetic biology.text: Synthetic biology (SynBio) is a multidisciplinary scientific field that applies the principles of engineering to develop new biological parts, devices, and systems or to redesign existing systems found in nature.

human milk.text: Breast milk or mother's milk is milk produced by the mammary glands in the breasts of humans.

fibrosis.text: Fibrosis, also known as fibrotic scarring, is the development of fibrous connective tissue in response to an injury.

structural vulnerability.text: Structural vulnerability is a term used in the fields of medical anthropology and public health to describe how social, economic, and political structures affect how certain individuals and populations have a higher risk of harm and poor health outcomes..

uk biobank.text: UK Biobank is a long-term prospective biobank study in the United Kingdom (UK) that houses the de-identified biological samples and health-related data of half a million people.

protoplanetary disk.text: A protoplanetary disk is a rotating circumstellar disc of dense gas and dust surrounding a young newly formed star, a T Tauri star, or Herbig Ae/Be star.

experiential learning.text: Experiential learning (ExL) is the process of learning through experience, and is more narrowly defined as "learning through reflection on doing".

geriatric care.text: Gerontological nursing is the specialty of nursing pertaining to older adults.

stereotypes.text: In social psychology, a stereotype is a generalized belief about a particular category of people.

air quality.text: Air pollution is the presence of substances in the air that are harmful to humans, other living beings or the environment.

panel data.text: In statistics and econometrics, panel data and longitudinal data are both multi-dimensional data involving measurements over time.

predictive coding.text: In neuroscience, psychology and cognitive science, predictive coding is a theory of brain function which postulates that the brain is constantly generating and updating a "mental model" of the environment.

obituary.text: An obituary is a biographical article written about someone who has recently died.

immunology.text: Immunology is a branch of biology and medicine that covers the study of immune systems in all organisms.

nerve fibers.text: A nerve is an enclosed, cable-like bundle of nerve fibers.

chemoimmunotherapy.text: Chemoimmunotherapy is chemotherapy combined with immunotherapy.

enceladus.text: Enceladus is the sixth-largest moon of Saturn and the 18th largest in the Solar System.

subsurface ocean.text: Planetary oceanography, also called astro-oceanography or exo-oceanography, is the study of oceans on planets and moons other than Earth.

orangutan.text: Orangutans are great apes native to the rainforests of Indonesia and Malaysia.

zero-emission.text: A zero emission engine, motor, process, or other energy source emits no waste products that pollute the environment or disrupt the climate.

belfast harbour.text: Belfast Harbour is a major maritime hub in Belfast, Northern Ireland, handling 67% of Northern Ireland's seaborne trade and about 25% of the maritime trade of the entire island of Ireland.

enteroendocrine cells.text: Enteroendocrine cells are specialized cells of the gastrointestinal tract and pancreas with endocrine function.

technology.text: Technology is the application of conceptual knowledge to achieve practical goals, especially in a reproducible way.

physics.text: Physics is the scientific study of matter, its fundamental constituents, its motion and behavior through space and time, and the related entities of energy and force.

post-stroke depression.text: Post-stroke depression (PSD) is a form of depression that may occur after a stroke.

convolutional neural networks.text: A convolutional neural network (CNN) is a type of feedforward neural network that learns features via filter optimization.

gilgamesh.text: Gilgamesh was a hero in ancient Mesopotamian mythology and the protagonist of the Epic of Gilgamesh, an epic poem written in Akkadian during the late 2nd millennium BC.

manichaeism.text: Manichaeism was a major world religion founded in the third century CE by the Parthian Iranian prophet Mani (216–274) in the Sasanian Empire.

feature selection.text: In machine learning, feature selection is the process of selecting a subset of relevant features for use in model construction.

indian ocean dipole.text: The Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) is an irregular oscillation of sea surface temperatures in which the western Indian Ocean becomes alternately warmer and then colder than the eastern part of the ocean.

enso.text: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is a global climate phenomenon that emerges from variation in winds and sea surface temperatures over the tropical Pacific Ocean.

linguistic distance.text: Linguistic distance is the measure of how different one language is from another.

second language acquisition.text: Second-language acquisition (SLA), second-language learning or L2 acquisition, is the process of learning a language other than one's native language (L1).

deep neural networks.text: In machine learning, deep learning (DL) focuses on utilizing multilayered neural networks to perform tasks such as classification, regression, and representation learning.

color perception.text: Color vision (CV), a feature of visual perception, is an ability to perceive differences between light composed of different frequencies independently of light intensity.

limited english proficiency.text: Limited English proficiency (LEP) is a term used in the United States that refers to a person who is not fluent in the English language, often because it is not their native language.

epidural.text: Epidural administration is a method of medication administration in which a medicine is injected into the epidural space around the spinal cord.

spinal headache.text: Post-dural-puncture headache (PDPH) is a complication of puncture of the dura mater.

deep vein thrombosis.text: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a type of venous thrombosis involving the formation of a blood clot in a deep vein, most commonly in the legs or pelvis.

growth hormone.text: Growth hormone (GH) or somatotropin, also known as human growth hormone in its human form, is a peptide hormone that stimulates growth, cell reproduction, and cell regeneration in humans and other animals.

deep sleep.text: Slow-wave sleep (SWS), often referred to as deep sleep, is the third stage of non-rapid eye movement sleep (NREM), where electroencephalography activity is characterised by slow delta waves.

major adverse cardiovascular events.text: Major adverse cardiovascular events is a composite endpoint frequently used in cardiovascular research.

gut health.text: Healthy digestion, also called digestive health, results in the absorption of nutrients from food without distressing symptoms.

animal models.text: A model organism is a non-human species that is extensively studied to understand particular biological phenomena, with the expectation that discoveries made in the model organism will provide insight into the workings of other organisms.

climate modeling.text: Numerical climate models are mathematical models that can simulate the interactions of important drivers of climate.

scientific publishing.text: Scientific literature encompasses a vast body of academic papers that spans various disciplines within the natural and social sciences.

retinitis pigmentosa.text: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is a member of a group of genetic disorders called inherited retinal dystrophy (IRD) that cause loss of vision.

starlink.text: Starlink Services, LLC is a telecommunications subsidiary of the American spaceflight company SpaceX, providing broadband Internet service in approximately 160 countries and territories.

satellite internet.text: Satellite Internet access is Internet access provided through communication satellites; if it can sustain high speeds, it is termed satellite broadband.

speed limits.text: Speed limits on road traffic, as used in most countries, set the legal maximum speed at which vehicles may travel on a given stretch of road.

thwaites glacier.text: Thwaites Glacier is an unusually broad and vast Antarctic glacier located east of Mount Murphy, on the Walgreen Coast of Marie Byrd Land.

computer model.text: Computer simulation is the running of a mathematical model on a computer, the model being designed to represent the behaviour of, or the outcome of, a real-world or physical system.

cardiothoracic surgery.text: Cardiothoracic (CT) surgery is the field of medicine involved in surgical treatment of organs inside the thoracic cavity — generally treatment of conditions of the heart, lungs, and other pleural or mediastinal structures.

epa.text: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is an independent agency of the United States government tasked with environmental protection matters.

heart valve replacement.text: Valve replacement is the surgical replacement of one or more of the heart valves with either an artificial heart valve or a bioprosthestic valve.

rabies.text: Rabies is a viral disease that causes inflammation of the brain in humans and other mammals.

post-exposure prophylaxis.text: Post-exposure prophylaxis, also known as post-exposure prevention (PEP), is any preventive medical treatment started after exposure to a pathogen in order to prevent the infection from occurring.

academic procrastination.text: Procrastination is an avoidance coping behavior that involves unnecessarily delaying or postponing something despite knowing that there could be negative consequences for doing so.

emergency severity index.text: The Emergency Severity Index (ESI) is a five-level emergency department triage algorithm, initially developed in 1998 by emergency physicians Richard Wurez and David Eitel, along with emergency nurses Nicki Gilboy, Taula Tanabe, and Debbie Travers.

inverse reinforcement learning.text: In machine learning and optimal control, reinforcement learning (RL) is concerned with how an intelligent agent should take actions in a dynamic environment in order to maximize a reward signal.

dental calculus.text: In dentistry, dental calculus or tartar is a form of hardened dental plaque.

causal inference.text: Causal inference is the process of determining the independent, actual effect of a particular phenomenon that is a component of a larger system.

weight stigma.text: Social stigma of obesity is bias or discriminatory behaviors targeted at overweight and obese individuals because of their weight and high body fat percentage.

cam plants.text: Crassulacean acid metabolism, also known as CAM photosynthesis, is a carbon fixation pathway that evolved in some plants as an adaptation to arid conditions that allows a plant to photosynthesize during the day, but only exchange gases at night.

metabolism.text: Metabolism refers to the set of life-sustaining chemical reactions that occur within living organisms.

hormone therapy.text: Hormone therapy or hormonal therapy is the use of hormones in medical treatment.

privacy.text: Privacy is the ability of an individual or group to seclude themselves or information about themselves, and thereby express themselves selectively.

quantum computer.text: A quantum computer is a computer that represents and processes information using quantum states.

grade.text: The GRADE approach is a method of assessing the certainty in evidence and the strength of recommendations in health care.

alpha-lactalbumin.text: α-lactalbumin, also known as alpha-lactalbumin and LALBA, is a protein that in humans is encoded by the LALBA gene.

tryptophan.text: Tryptophan (symbol Trp or W), historically also known as tryptophane, is an α-amino acid that is used in the biosynthesis of proteins.

publication bias.text: In published academic research, publication bias occurs when the outcome of an experiment or research study biases the decision to publish or otherwise distribute it.

informal carer.text: A caregiver, caretaker or direct care worker is a person who provides physical, emotional or personal care for people who can not function independently due to age, chronic illness, injury or disability.

neglected tropical diseases.text: Neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) are a diverse group of tropical infections that are common in low-income populations in developing regions of Africa, Asia, and the Americas.

postpartum depression.text: Postpartum depression (PPD), from Latin post partum, also known as perinatal depression, is a mood disorder which may be experienced by pregnant or postpartum women.

post-training.text: Post-training of large language models is a term used in recent technical literature for training applied to a large language model (LLM) after its initial large-scale pretraining.

ensemble learning.text: In statistics and machine learning, ensemble methods use multiple learning algorithms to obtain better predictive performance than could be obtained from any of the constituent learning algorithms alone.

problematic internet use.text: Internet addiction disorder (IAD), also called problematic Internet use (PIU), is characterized by excessive or poorly controlled preoccupations, urges, or behaviors regarding computer use and Internet access that lead to impairment or distress.

dopamine.text: Dopamine is a neuromodulatory molecule that plays several important roles in cells.

associative learning.text: Learning is the process of acquiring new understanding, knowledge, behavior, skills, values, attitudes, and preferences.

items.title: Children and Adolescents' Mental Health

ai.headline: Many young people have mental health disorders but most do not get help.
ai.summary: The paper reviews evidence on children's and adolescents' mental health, noting that early adverse experiences can increase the likelihood of mental illness. It states that globally 8% of children and 15% of adolescents face a mental disorder, yet most do not seek or receive treatment.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding that mental health struggles are common among young people can help reduce stigma and encourage seeking support.
ai.life_skill: Notice if you or someone you know is struggling and speak to a trusted adult or qualified professional.
ai.fact: Suicide is the third most common cause of death among people aged 15 to 29.

quiz.question: What percentage of adolescents globally face a mental disorder according to the paper?
quiz.answer: The paper states that 15% of adolescents face a mental disorder.

ai.caveat: The abstract describes a meta-analysis of randomized trials but does not report specific results or effect sizes from those trials.

items.title: Effectiveness of Wrist-Worn Wearable-Guided Cardiac Rehabilitation Delivered Through Fully Remote or Hybrid Programs in Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

ai.headline: Wearable-guided remote cardiac rehab may boost fitness and activity, but results are inconsistent across settings.
ai.summary: This systematic review of 18 randomised trials looked at wrist-worn wearable-guided cardiac rehabilitation delivered fully remotely or in hybrid form for people with cardiovascular disease. It found average improvements in peak oxygen uptake, six-minute walk distance and daily steps, but prediction intervals included no effect, meaning benefits may not hold in every future setting.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how remote, wearable-supported rehab could help more people with heart disease stay active outside clinic-based programmes.
ai.life_skill: Try using a wrist-worn activity tracker to monitor your daily steps and set gradual movement goals if you are managing a heart condition, after checking with your healthcare team.
ai.fact: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide.

quiz.question: What did the review find about the consistency of benefits across future settings?
quiz.answer: The prediction intervals included no effect, indicating uncertainty about whether benefits will be consistent in comparable future settings.

ai.caveat: The multicomponent nature of the programmes means effects cannot be attributed to wearables alone, and all prediction intervals included the null.

items.title: Diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence in early diagnosis of mosquito-borne viral infections: Systematic review and meta-analysis

ai.headline: AI models show promising early diagnosis of mosquito-borne viruses, but evidence is uneven and biased.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 43 studies on artificial intelligence for early diagnosis of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. Reported accuracy and other performance measures were high, but most studies were at high risk of bias, focused on dengue in Asia, and lacked external validation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows AI could one day help spot these infections sooner, but current results are not yet reliable enough for routine use everywhere.
ai.life_skill: Check that any health app or AI diagnostic tool you use has been independently tested and validated before trusting its results.
ai.fact: Most AI studies for early diagnosis of mosquito-borne viral infections focused on dengue and were conducted in Asia.

quiz.question: What did the review find about the quality of the AI studies?
quiz.answer: Most studies were at high overall risk of bias, and calibration and external validation were uncommon.

ai.caveat: The pooled results are descriptive summaries of a highly heterogeneous evidence base, not proof of real-world performance.

items.title: Obstructive sleep apnea and long COVID syndrome: a scoping review of current evidence in adults

ai.headline: Sleep apnoea may be linked to long COVID, but the direction and cause are still unclear.
ai.summary: A scoping review of 11 studies looked at adults with obstructive sleep apnoea and long COVID. It found an association between the two, with symptoms such as fatigue, breathing problems, cognitive difficulties and cardiovascular issues reported, but the nature and direction of the link vary across studies.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights that sleep health could matter for recovery after COVID-19, though more research is needed before firm conclusions can be drawn.
ai.life_skill: Notice how well you sleep and discuss ongoing tiredness or breathing problems with a qualified health professional.
ai.fact: Obstructive sleep apnoea involves interrupted breathing during sleep and can cause sleep fragmentation and low oxygen levels.

quiz.question: What did the review find about the link between sleep apnoea and long COVID?
quiz.answer: It found an association between them, but the direction and causality remain uncertain.

ai.caveat: The review is based on a small number of heterogeneous studies and cannot prove that sleep apnoea causes long COVID or that treating it improves long COVID outcomes.

items.title: What Helps or Hinders Therapeutic Relationships in Inpatient Mental Healthcare: a Systematic Review to Inform Policy and Practice

ai.headline: Staff empathy, consistent time together, shared power and welcoming ward spaces help build good therapeutic relationships on mental health wards.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 184 studies involving nearly 20,000 people to see what helps or harms relationships between staff and service users on inpatient mental health wards. It found that reducing power imbalances, staff showing empathy and treating people as individuals, having consistent staff with time to connect, and ward environments that allow interaction all support positive relationships, while restrictive practices and task-focused, risk-focused ward cultures weaken them.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how everyday interactions and ward environments shape the quality of care people receive when they are most vulnerable.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether staff treat you as an individual rather than just a patient, and ask for time to talk if you feel rushed.
ai.fact: Therapeutic relationships between service users and staff on inpatient mental health wards are central to high-quality care.

quiz.question: What did the review find helps build positive relationships on inpatient mental health wards?
quiz.answer: Staff relational skills such as empathy and non-judgemental approaches, staff continuity and time to connect, reduced power imbalances, and ward environments that create opportunities for interaction.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and it synthesises many different study designs rather than proving cause and effect.

items.title: Familial factors inflate the estimated effects of genetic liability to ADHD on behavioural outcomes

ai.headline: Family background may explain much of the harm linked to ADHD, not ADHD itself.
ai.summary: Researchers compared population-wide results with results from siblings to separate a person’s own ADHD from shared family factors. The links between genetic liability to ADHD and smoking, alcohol use, depressive symptoms, lower education, earlier first child and weaker cognitive performance mostly disappeared in the sibling analysis.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that some problems blamed on ADHD may actually come from the family environment, so treating the individual alone may not fix them.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether difficulties you attribute to a diagnosis might also be shaped by your family or home environment.
ai.fact: Genetic liability to ADHD is linked to several health and behavioural outcomes in population studies, but those links weaken when family factors are accounted for.

quiz.question: What happened to the estimated effect of ADHD genetic liability on depressive symptoms when researchers compared siblings instead of the whole population?
quiz.answer: It fell from 0.059 SD to 0.002 SD, suggesting little or no direct effect once family factors were considered.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Biology and Benefits of Music Play and Stories for Kids/Parents During ALL Treatment

ai.headline: A trial is testing whether active music engagement lowers stress hormones in children with leukaemia and their parents.
ai.summary: This randomised trial studies an Active Music Engagement intervention during consolidation treatment for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia. It aims to see whether it lowers cortisol, a stress biomarker, in children and parents, and whether cortisol explains any benefits.
ai.why_it_matters: It could show how music might support wellbeing during serious illness beyond just mood.
ai.life_skill: Try listening to or making music when you feel stressed to see if it helps you feel calmer.
ai.fact: Cortisol is a hormone linked to stress in the body.

quiz.question: What stress biomarker is this trial measuring?
quiz.answer: The trial is measuring cortisol.

ai.caveat: This is a trial record with planned aims, not yet published results showing whether the intervention worked.

items.title: Beyond social skills: emotion regulation as a potential mechanism linking physical exercise to social anxiety in left-behind adolescents

ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI could help doctors assess bowel disease more consistently and support decisions in clinical trials.
ai.fact: Active ulcerative colitis tissue had about twice the neutrophil density in the lamina propria and over five times the neutrophil density in crypts compared with remission tissue.

quiz.question: What did active ulcerative colitis biopsies show compared with remission biopsies?
quiz.answer: They showed higher neutrophil and lymphocyte densities and more crypt injury, including mucin depletion, branching and abscesses.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed and was evaluated in a single clinical network, so the findings need independent validation.

items.title: Acceptability and Efficacy of Pain Reprocessing Therapy in Racially/ Ethnically Diverse Adults With Chronic Back Pain

ai.summary: This clinical trial compares Pain Reprocessing Therapy (PRT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and usual care for chronic back pain. ai.fact: Chronic back pain is a common condition that can have various treatments

items.title: Independent predictors of non-suicidal self-injury among adolescents: a logistic regression model development study based on coping styles

ai.headline: Self-blame is linked to higher odds of adolescent self-injury, while problem-solving skills are linked to lower odds.
ai.summary: A cross-sectional study of 206 adolescents compared 104 who self-injured without suicidal intent with 102 healthy controls. Higher self-blame was an independent risk factor, while better problem-solving capacity was linked to lower odds. The researchers built a nomogram to help distinguish between groups.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights coping styles that may matter for understanding and preventing self-injury among teenagers.
ai.life_skill: Notice when you blame yourself and try to break the problem into small, manageable steps instead.
ai.fact: Self-blame was independently associated with non-suicidal self-injury in this adolescent sample.

quiz.answer: A higher level of self-blame was an independent risk factor.

items.title: Bayes-Adaptive MDPs for Rollout Allocation to Enhance GRPO Training

ai.headline: A new AI training method gives harder questions more practice rolls without extra cost.
ai.summary: The study looked at how AI models learn from reasoning questions using a method called GRPO. It found that giving more training attempts to harder questions, while using fewer on easier ones, improves learning under the same total budget.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how smarter allocation of limited computing effort can make AI training more efficient.
ai.life_skill: Try spending more practice time on the topics you find hardest rather than splitting your time evenly.
ai.fact: Adaptive rollout allocation can improve GRPO training performance on reasoning tasks under a fixed budget.

quiz.question: What does AdaRoll-GRPO do differently from standard GRPO?
quiz.answer: It allocates more rollouts to harder questions and fewer to easier ones while keeping the total budget the same.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?

ai.headline: Code can describe videos better than words, but AI still struggles to write that code.
ai.summary: Researchers tested whether computer code could describe videos more accurately than natural language. Code captions performed better on question-answering and video reconstruction tasks. Today's AI models still struggle to write faithful code captions, especially for complex timing.
ai.why_it_matters: This shows a new way AI might understand and recreate video, though it is not yet reliable enough for everyday use.
ai.fact: Code-based captions can preserve video information more accurately than natural-language captions for some tasks.

quiz.question: How did code captions compare with natural language captions?
quiz.answer: Code captions achieved superior reasoning accuracy and video reconstruction fidelity.

ai.caveat: This is a single preprint that has not been peer reviewed, so the results are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Impairment of mental time travel in patients with depressive disorders: Neural mechanisms and individual-level identification based on default mode network connectivity

ai.headline: People with depression show altered brain network connections linked to poorer memory and future thinking.
ai.summary: Researchers compared 36 people with major depressive disorder and 36 healthy controls using memory tests and brain scans. Those with depression recalled past events and imagined future events with less detail, less positive emotion, weaker perspective and lower intensity, and showed specific changes in default mode network connectivity.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how depression may affect the ability to remember the past and imagine the future, which are important for everyday planning and wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Notice when recalling the past or imagining the future feels vague or overly negative, and consider discussing it with a qualified mental health professional.
ai.fact: Mental time travel lets people re-experience the past and pre-experience future events.

quiz.question: What did people with major depressive disorder show compared with healthy controls in this study?
quiz.answer: They had reduced specificity in recalling the past and imagining the future, with lower emotional valence, field perspective and intensity.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, involved a small sample, and cannot prove that brain connections cause the memory and imagination differences.

items.title: American jobs offer more autonomy—and more stress

ai.headline: US jobs have grown more stressful over 20 years while giving workers more independence.
ai.summary: The piece reports on trends in American jobs over the past two decades. It finds that work has become increasingly stressful, but employees have also gained more ability to make decisions and act independently.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that greater control at work can come alongside higher stress, which matters for how people think about job quality and wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether having more control over your tasks changes how stressful your work feels.
ai.fact: American jobs have become more stressful over the past two decades while offering workers more independence.

quiz.question: What two trends does the article report for American jobs over the past 20 years?
quiz.answer: Jobs have become more stressful, and workers have gained more independence and decision-making ability.

items.title: Towards understanding stomatal decoupling under extreme heat: integrating stomatal kinetics, leaf light responses, and the role of stomatal versus cuticular conductance

ai.headline: Some tree species keep their stomata open in extreme heat, losing water faster than expected.
ai.summary: Researchers exposed two rainforest and two semi-arid tree species to heat and drought in a glasshouse. Stomatal decoupling—where stomata stay open despite heat—happened in two species, including the most drought-tolerant one, but not in a vulnerable rainforest species. Water loss happened mainly through open stomata rather than the leaf surface, and stomata opened faster and closed more slowly at 34°C than at 25°C.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain why some forests die during hotter droughts while others survive, improving predictions of how trees cope with climate change.
ai.life_skill: Notice how different plants respond to hot weather and avoid assuming all trees handle heat the same way.
ai.fact: Stomata can open faster and close more slowly at higher leaf temperatures, affecting how much water a tree loses.

quiz.question: Through what route did accelerated leaf water loss mainly occur during heat stress?
quiz.answer: It occurred predominantly through open stomata rather than through the cuticle.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, based on a small glasshouse experiment with four tree species, so the findings are not yet confirmed or widely generalisable.

items.title: Scientists discover a hidden 100-million-year-old volcanic system

ai.headline: Scientists found a 100-million-year-old volcanic system hidden in Iran.
ai.summary: Researchers studied ancient rocks in Iran and uncovered a volcanic system dating back about 100 million years. The discovery reveals new details about how an ancient ocean disappeared and how geological forces reshaped the Middle East.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps us understand how Earth’s surface changes over millions of years and how continents and oceans have moved.
ai.fact: A volcanic system about 100 million years old has been identified in Iran.

quiz.question: How old is the volcanic system discovered in Iran?
quiz.answer: It dates back roughly 100 million years.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not the original peer-reviewed research, so the details have not been independently verified here.

items.title: Modalities and dosage of exercise interventions for improving adolescent mental health: a systematic review and meta-analysis

ai.headline: Exercise can reduce depression, anxiety and stress in teenagers, with different types and amounts possibly helping different symptoms.
ai.summary: Researchers combined 17 randomised controlled trials of exercise programmes for adolescents. Exercise was linked to lower depression, anxiety and stress compared with control groups. The review suggests low-intensity TCC under three times a week for over 60 minutes may help generally, HIIT over 60 minutes under three times a week may help anxiety, and yoga for 30–60 minutes under three times a week may help stress.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that regular physical activity may be a useful, non-drug way to support teenage mental wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Try doing gentle movement such as yoga or tai chi a couple of times a week and notice whether your mood feels steadier.
ai.fact: Exercise interventions were linked to significant reductions in depression, anxiety and stress among adolescents in the included trials.

quiz.question: What did the review find about exercise and adolescent mental health?
quiz.answer: Exercise was linked to significant improvements in depression, anxiety and stress compared with control groups.

ai.caveat: The review included only 17 trials, results varied widely across studies, and publication bias cannot be ruled out, so the specific exercise recommendations should be treated as tentative.

items.title: Ergonomic interventions for treating work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder in adults.
items.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

ai.headline: Ergonomic changes may make little or no difference to arm, neck or shoulder pain in the short term.
ai.summary: This Cochrane review looked at 20 studies involving 2478 adults with work-related arm, neck or shoulder complaints. It found ergonomic interventions may result in little to no difference in pain, functional status or sick leave compared with no treatment, usual care or placebo in the short term.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps people understand that adjusting a workstation alone may not quickly reduce work-related aches or time off work.
ai.life_skill: Try adjusting your desk, chair or equipment for comfort, but do not expect it by itself to cure arm, neck or shoulder pain.
ai.fact: Work-related complaints of the arm, neck or shoulder can develop from repetitive movements, awkward postures or external forces such as vibrating tools.

quiz.question: What did the review find about ergonomic interventions and pain in the short term?
quiz.answer: They may result in little to no difference in pain compared with no treatment, usual care or placebo.

ai.caveat: The evidence is mostly low- to moderate-certainty and the abstract cuts off before reporting all results.

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of recommended interventions for managing low back pain: A systematic review.

ai.headline: Non-drug, non-surgical low back pain treatments such as exercise, acupuncture and self-management support can be cost-effective compared with usual care.
ai.summary: The researchers reviewed 20 studies of guideline-recommended non-pharmacological, non-surgical treatments for low back pain. Most were cost-effective at a £20,000-per-QALY threshold, and some—including yoga, acupuncture, cognitive therapy and self-management support—were both more effective and less costly than usual care.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows which everyday back-pain options may offer better value for money, helping people and health services choose treatments that work without unnecessary cost.
ai.life_skill: Try asking a qualified health professional about exercise, self-management support or psychological support for ongoing low back pain instead of assuming medication or surgery is the only option.
ai.fact: Low back pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide.

quiz.question: What did most of the reviewed low back pain interventions have in common regarding cost-effectiveness?
quiz.answer: Most interventions were cost-effective at a willingness-to-pay threshold of £20,000 per quality-adjusted life year.

ai.caveat: All the evidence came from high-income countries and was heterogeneous, so findings may not apply to low- and middle-income settings.

items.title: Factors Affecting Work Productivity and Activity Impairment in Axial Spondyloarthritis Patients

ai.headline: Axial spondyloarthritis is linked to high unemployment and activity impairment in Bangladeshi adults.
ai.summary: This cross-sectional study of 222 adults with axial spondyloarthritis found that 38.7% were unemployed and activity impairment was higher among unemployed participants. ai.why_it_matters: It shows how a chronic inflammatory condition can affect work and daily activity during economically productive years.

ai.fact: In this study, 38.7% of participants with axial spondyloarthritis were unemployed.

items.title: The effects of non-pharmacological school-based interventions on educational outcomes in children and young people with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a meta-analysis

ai.headline: School-based support may slightly improve educational outcomes for young people with ADHD, but results are mixed.
ai.summary: The study reviewed 16 randomised trials of school-based interventions for children and young people aged 5–17 with ADHD. Overall, the interventions showed a small effect on educational outcomes, but no specific type of intervention or outcome stood out as clearly better.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that schools can offer support for students with ADHD, but there is not yet enough clear evidence to know which approaches work best.

ai.fact: A meta-analysis combines results from multiple studies to look for an overall pattern.

quiz.question: What did the meta-analysis find about school-based interventions for young people with ADHD?
quiz.answer: Overall they showed a small effect on educational outcomes, but no particular intervention type or outcome domain was clearly better.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the included studies varied so much that the overall pattern is inconclusive.

items.title: Criterion validity of device-based motion sensors for monitoring free-living physical activity in community-dwelling manual wheelchair users: A systematic review
items.venue: European Journal of Adapted Physical Activity

ai.headline: Motion sensors can accurately track physical activity in people who use manual wheelchairs.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 40 studies of 34 devices that measure movement in manual wheelchair users. Sensors worn on the body or mounted on the wheelchair gave accurate estimates of energy use, self-propulsion, other activities, and wheelchair time, distance and speed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how activity can be measured fairly in wheelchair users, helping them and services track movement and health.
ai.life_skill: Try noticing how much you move each day, whether by wheelchair or otherwise, as part of everyday health.
ai.fact: Manual wheelchair users tend to be less active and more sedentary than people who walk.

quiz.question: What did the review find about body-worn tri-axial accelerometers on the upper arm or wrist?

ai.caveat: The evidence quality varied, with many devices rated low or very low, and the authors call for better-quality research.

items.title: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions

ai.headline: A new training method helps AI models see images more accurately by rewarding correct visual details.
ai.summary: The study tested PerceptRL, a way to train multimodal large language models to improve fine-grained visual perception. It converts verified errors from image captions into question-and-answer tasks with rule-based rewards, and adds multi-turn visual inspection for complex cases. On seven benchmarks, it improved average accuracy by 15.7 percentage points over a base model with the same tools.
ai.why_it_matters: Better AI vision could make everyday tools like image search and accessibility apps more reliable.
ai.life_skill: Check that AI descriptions of images match what you can actually see before relying on them.
ai.fact: PerceptRL surpassed the strongest evaluated frontier vision-language model by 5.2 percentage points on average accuracy across seven benchmarks.

quiz.answer: It converted verified visual errors into QA pairs with fixed answer labels and rule-based rewards.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: A Polygenic Score for Smoking Persistence Captures Differences in Cessation Age

ai.headline: A genetic score linked to smoking persistence is associated with later quitting age across diverse groups.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 139,129 current and former smokers and compared those with the highest and lowest genetic scores for smoking persistence. People in the highest decile had an estimated median cessation age of 48 years versus 40 years in the lowest decile, an 8-year difference after adjustment.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how genetic liability may help identify people who could benefit from earlier, targeted support to stop smoking.

items.title: Cumulative heatwave exposure and cognitive ageing in Chinese middle-aged and older adults: educational vulnerability and urban concentration in a five-wave national cohort

ai.headline: More heatwave days are linked to faster cognitive decline in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, especially those with less education and urban residents.
ai.summary: Researchers followed over 13,000 Chinese adults aged 45 and older across five survey waves from 2011 to 2020. They found that each additional 10 heatwave days over the previous three years was linked to greater cognitive decline that grew stronger with age, with the effect concentrated among less-educated and urban participants.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how extreme heat may affect thinking skills as people age, highlighting groups that might need extra support during hot weather.

ai.fact: Heatwave days were defined as at least three consecutive days above the 92.5th percentile of the 1986–2005 temperature climatology.

quiz.question: Which group showed stronger heat-related cognitive ageing in the study?
quiz.answer: Less-educated adults and urban residents showed steeper heat-related cognitive ageing than others.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and as an observational study it cannot prove that heatwaves caused the cognitive decline.

items.title: Metabolomics in the wild: A scoping review of non-invasive methods for understanding vertebrate wildlife health and success

ai.headline: Scientists are increasingly using non-invasive samples to study the chemistry of wild vertebrate animals.
ai.summary: A scoping review of 83 peer-reviewed papers found that non-invasive metabolomics research on wild vertebrates has grown rapidly, with over 60% published between 2022 and 2025. The research covered 93 species, mostly mammals, and focused mainly on physiology, reproduction, diet and nutrition.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how new, animal-friendly lab techniques are helping conservationists understand wildlife health without harming the animals.
ai.life_skill: Notice how scientists study wild animals using samples like droppings or feathers instead of taking blood.

quiz.answer: Over 60% of all publications were published between 2022 and 2025.

ai.caveat: This is a scoping review summarising existing observational studies, so it maps the field rather than proving a single cause-and-effect finding.

items.title: University at Buffalo Campus Veggie Van Mobile Market

ai.headline: A mobile produce market on a university campus aims to improve student access to fresh fruit and vegetables.
ai.summary: This observational study will pilot a mobile market at the University at Buffalo to learn what stops students eating healthy foods, how to run the market to reach students, and whether using it is linked to eating more fruit and vegetables, better food security, and SNAP participation.

items.title: MoveBench: A Rubric-Based Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Sports and Health Coaching

ai.headline: AI chatbots vary widely in how safely they coach sport and health, a new benchmark finds.
ai.summary: Researchers created MoveBench, a test for large language models in sports and health coaching. ai.why_it_matters: It shows that AI fitness and health advice can be inconsistent or unsafe, so people should not rely on chatbots alone for coaching.

items.title: scTGCL: A Transformer-Based Graph Contrastive Learning Approach for Efficiently Clustering Single-Cell RNA-seq Data

ai.headline: A new computer method groups single cells more accurately by learning patterns in gene activity data.
ai.summary: The study tested scTGCL, a Transformer-based graph contrastive learning tool, on twenty real and simulated single-cell RNA sequencing datasets. ai.why_it_matters: It helps scientists understand cell types and biological processes more reliably, which can improve research into health and disease.
ai.fact: Single-cell RNA sequencing measures gene activity in individual cells to reveal cellular diversity.

quiz.question: What did scTGCL do better than nine existing methods across twenty datasets?
quiz.answer: It achieved higher clustering accuracy, normalized mutual information, and adjusted Rand index, plus better imputation and faster runtime on large datasets.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are preliminary and not yet confirmed.

items.title: Comparative Advantage and Economies of Scale under Uncertainty -- by Xiao Ma, Natalia Ramondo

ai.headline: Uncertainty and economies of scale reduce the gains from trade by shifting jobs away from riskier places and sectors.
ai.summary: The paper uses a model of regional economies to study how uncertainty and economies of scale affect where people work and how much they gain from trade. It finds that uncertainty pushes employment away from riskier sectors and locations, lowering overall gains from trade by around 20 percent. Agglomeration forces and flexible labour supply can soften losses for regions that would otherwise lose from trade.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain why economic shocks can reshape local job markets and why the benefits of trade are smaller when the future is uncertain.
ai.life_skill: Notice how uncertainty in your local job market might affect your career choices and consider building flexible skills.
ai.fact: Uncertainty shifts employment away from riskier sectors and locations relative to a deterministic benchmark.

quiz.question: By roughly what percentage does uncertainty lower the U.S. aggregate gains from trade in the study?
quiz.answer: Around 20 percent.

items.title: The autistic brain processes faces differently than scientists thought

items.title: Workplace ergonomics may do little to ease arm, neck or shoulder pain

ai.headline: Ergonomic changes at work may not meaningfully reduce arm, neck or shoulder pain.
ai.summary: An updated Cochrane review looked at ergonomic interventions for workers with arm, neck or shoulder complaints. It found no meaningful benefit for pain, function, recovery or sick leave compared with no treatment.

items.title: DNA analysis identifies root-dwelling fungi as potential keystone species in forest microbial communities

ai.headline: DNA analysis suggests root-dwelling fungi may be keystone species in forest soil ecosystems.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed DNA from soil and root systems to study microbial communities in forests. They identified root-dwelling fungi as potential keystone species that disproportionately influence nutrient cycling and carbon sequestration.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding which organisms hold ecosystems together helps explain how forests store carbon and recycle nutrients.
ai.life_skill: Notice how removing one small part of a system can have large, unexpected effects on the whole.

quiz.answer: They exert a disproportionately large influence on the entire structure and function of the ecosystem.

items.title: The Relationship between Students' Perceptions and Their Engagement through Self-Regulated Learning

ai.headline: Students who manage their own learning better engage more in difficult statistics classes.
ai.summary: This study surveyed 533 psychology students in Indonesia to see how teacher creativity and self-regulation affect engagement in statistics. items.title: A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength

items.title: Devastating 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami left victims more prone to obesity, heart disease

ai.headline: Survivors of the 2004 tsunami may face higher risks of obesity and heart disease years later.
ai.summary: The report describes a study of people affected by the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. It found that victims were more prone to obesity and heart disease, adding to evidence that traumatic experiences are linked to poorer health years later.

ai.fact: Traumatic experiences are linked to health problems such as obesity and heart disease years later.
