ai.headline: A small palliative-care course helped health and social care students learn teamwork and reflect on their professional roles using stories.
ai.summary: Researchers evaluated a storyline-based interprofessional palliative care course with 25 students from medicine, nursing, social work, and religious education at one German university. Students reported high satisfaction and gains in social and communication skills, knowledge of other professions, and team problem-solving, though they wanted more balanced professional representation and real clinical experiences.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how story-based learning can help future health and social care workers understand each other’s roles and work together better.
ai.life_skill: Notice how different professionals contribute to a team and ask about their roles rather than assuming you know them.
ai.fact: Interprofessional education aims to help students from different health and social care professions learn with, from, and about each other.

quiz.question: What did students particularly rate positively in the survey?
quiz.answer: They rated social and communication skills, knowledge of other professional groups, and team-oriented problem solving especially positively.

ai.caveat: This was a small, single-course evaluation without a control group, so the results cannot prove the curriculum caused the improvements.

items.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems

ai.headline: AI agents can accidentally reveal secrets by combining harmless pieces of information they find online.
ai.summary: Researchers tested AI agents that read documents and answer questions. Even when questions seemed safe, the agents sometimes combined details from different documents to reveal confidential information, despite safeguards like warning labels and rules against sharing.
ai.why_it_matters: This shows that AI tools used at work or school might leak private information without meaning to, so people need to be careful about what they share with them.
ai.life_skill: Check what personal or confidential information you share with AI assistants before asking them to summarise or combine documents.
ai.fact: AI agents can disclose sensitive conclusions by piecing together separate pieces of information, even when each piece seems harmless on its own.

quiz.question: What did the researchers find about AI agents and confidential information?
quiz.answer: AI agents sometimes combined separate pieces of information to reveal confidential conclusions, even when questions seemed safe and safeguards were in place.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the results come from simulated and live agent tests rather than real-world use.

items.title: How does community of inquiry matter? Mediating effects and configurational pathways linking project-based learning design to learning engagement

ai.headline: Project-based learning boosts engagement
ai.summary: Researchers studied project-based learning in animation students using generative AI. They found that certain design elements and community of inquiry factors are linked to learning engagement. The study identified configurations of factors that support high engagement.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how to design effective project-based learning experiences can help educators boost student engagement and motivation
ai.life_skill: Try incorporating community of inquiry principles into your learning activities
ai.fact: Project-based learning design elements, such as problem-driven and project implementation, are linked to learning engagement

quiz.question: What was the context of the research study?
quiz.answer: The study was set in AIGC-assisted project-based learning studios for animation students

ai.caveat: The study's conclusions are limited to AIGC-assisted project-based learning studios and do not establish causality between the design elements and learning engagement

items.title: Diagnosing the Explicit-to-Applied Theory of Mind Gap in LLMs

ai.headline: AI models struggle with social cognition
ai.summary: Researchers studied large language models' social cognition using Theory of Mind benchmarks. They found that aggregate scores hide uneven competence in recognizing mental states and predicting behavior. The study investigated the gap between explicit and applied Theory of Mind and its recoverability using various interventions.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because large language models are being used in high-stakes roles such as therapy and education, where social cognition is crucial.
ai.life_skill: Try to consider the limitations of AI models when interacting with them.
ai.fact: Large language models can recognize mental states but struggle to predict behavior based on those states.

quiz.question: What do current Theory of Mind benchmarks conflate?
quiz.answer: Explicit and applied Theory of Mind competencies.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint study that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: Affirming and Undermining Motivations and Adolescents' Reading Comprehension: Moderator Effects of Reading Level and Motivation-Enhancing Educational Characteristics

ai.headline: Motivation affects reading comprehension
ai.summary: Researchers studied the relationship between motivation and reading comprehension in 3390 Dutch 15-year-olds. They found that positive motivations were linked to better reading comprehension, while negative motivations were linked to poorer comprehension. The study also examined the role of educational characteristics in moderating this relationship.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding the relationship between motivation and reading comprehension can help educators develop effective strategies to improve reading skills in students.
ai.life_skill: Try to identify and address negative motivations that may be hindering your reading progress.
ai.fact: Positive motivations, such as intrinsic motivation and perception of competence, are linked to better reading comprehension.

quiz.question: What type of motivations were found to be linked to poorer reading comprehension?
quiz.answer: Undermining motivations, such as avoidance and perceived difficulty in reading.

ai.caveat: The study's findings are based on a single observational study and may not be causal, highlighting the need for further experimental and longitudinal research.

items.title: Putting conversational AI to the test in primary care

ai.headline: A patient-facing conversational AI was found feasible and safe in one primary care clinic.
ai.summary: The study tested a conversational AI tool for patients in a single primary care setting. It found the tool showed promising feasibility and safety, supporting larger-scale evaluation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI might one day be used safely in everyday healthcare, though more research is needed before it becomes routine.
ai.life_skill: Try asking a qualified health professional before relying on AI for medical questions.
ai.fact: A patient-facing conversational AI showed promising feasibility and safety in a single-center primary care setting.

quiz.question: Where was the conversational AI tested?
quiz.answer: It was tested in a single-center primary care setting.

ai.caveat: The findings come from one center only and are not yet proof that the AI works broadly or for everyone.

items.title: Scientists discover a surprising secret behind the human brain’s wrinkles

ai.headline: Small changes to brain-building cells may explain why marmoset brains stay smooth while human brains fold.
ai.summary: Researchers studied common marmosets, whose brains are unusually small and smooth despite developing like other primates early on. They found that subtle changes to brain-building cells slow neuron production, offering clues about how the large, folded human brain evolved.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps us understand how human brains became large and folded, which underlies our thinking abilities.
ai.fact: Common marmosets have unusually small, smooth brains despite starting development much like other primates.

quiz.question: What did researchers find about marmoset brain-building cells?
quiz.answer: Subtle changes to these cells slow neuron production, which may explain their small, smooth brains.

ai.caveat: The study was in marmosets, not humans, so it cannot prove how human brains evolved.

items.title: A third of young adults turn to AI for substance-use information

ai.headline: Over 32% of young adults in a Rutgers study used AI chatbots for substance-use information.
ai.summary: A Rutgers study asked young adults whether they used AI chatbots such as ChatGPT for substance-use information. More than 32% said they had.
ai.why_it_matters: Many young people are turning to AI for health-related information, so it matters whether those tools give safe and accurate answers.
ai.life_skill: Check substance-use information from an AI chatbot against a trusted health source or a qualified professional.
ai.fact: More than 32% of participants in the Rutgers study reported using ChatGPT and similar chatbots for substance-use information.

quiz.question: What percentage of participants in the Rutgers study reported using AI chatbots for substance-use information?
quiz.answer: More than 32% reported using ChatGPT and similar chatbots for substance-use information.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a single study, not peer-reviewed evidence, and it does not give details about how the study was designed or who took part.

items.title: Association Between Exercise and Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) Levels in Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

ai.headline: Exercise may raise BDNF levels in people with diabetes, but evidence is limited.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis looked at four trials involving 131 people with diabetes. It found that serum BDNF levels were higher in people who exercised compared with controls, though the result was only borderline statistically significant. Exercise did not significantly change body weight, body fat percentage, or fasting blood glucose.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests exercise might support brain health in people with diabetes, but more research is needed before firm conclusions can be drawn.
ai.life_skill: Try regular physical activity as part of a healthy routine, but discuss any new exercise plan with a qualified health professional if you have diabetes.
ai.fact: BDNF is a protein in the nervous system that plays a crucial role in the development of brain circuits.

quiz.question: Did exercise significantly change body weight or fasting blood glucose in people with diabetes according to this review?
quiz.answer: No, body weight and fasting blood glucose showed no statistically significant differences between exercise and control groups.

ai.caveat: Only four small trials with 131 participants were included, and the authors say larger studies are needed to confirm the findings.

items.title: Psychoeducation for posttraumatic stress disorder in adults: a systematic review of formats and delivery approaches

ai.headline: Digital psychoeducation with human guidance may reduce PTSD symptoms, but evidence is mixed and not strong enough to use alone.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 26 randomised trials involving 3,304 adults looked at psychoeducation for posttraumatic stress disorder. Nine trials found significant symptom reductions, all using digital delivery and most with human guidance, but overall effects were inconsistent and several positive trials had a high risk of bias.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that low-cost digital information can be a helpful first step toward care, but it should not replace professional treatment for PTSD.
ai.life_skill: If you or someone you know has experienced trauma, consider using a reputable digital psychoeducation resource as a first step while arranging support from a qualified mental health professional.
ai.fact: Psychoeducation is described as a low-cost and accessible entry point to care for PTSD.
ai.caveat: The review was not prospectively registered, the evidence was of limited methodological quality, and several positive trials had some concerns or a high risk of bias.

items.title: Role of Nutrition Therapy in Prediabetes: A Systematic Review

ai.headline: Structured diets may improve blood sugar and weight in adults with prediabetes, but no single diet is best.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at ten randomised trials involving 1,098 adults with prediabetes. Calorie-restricted and low-carbohydrate diets were linked to weight loss and better blood sugar measures, while low-glycaemic-index, Mediterranean, high-protein, and intermittent fasting diets showed some benefits for insulin sensitivity, fasting glucose, ectopic fat, or weight.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that changing what you eat may help prevent type 2 diabetes, though the best approach varies from person to person.
ai.life_skill: Try swapping refined carbohydrates for higher-fibre, lower-glycaemic-index foods and speak with a qualified health professional before making major dietary changes.
ai.fact: Prediabetes is a critical window for diabetes intervention.

quiz.question: What did the review conclude about which diet is best for prediabetes?
quiz.answer: No single dietary strategy emerged as universally optimal.

ai.caveat: The review included only ten small, varied trials with some risk-of-bias concerns, so the findings are not definitive.

items.title: Neurospirituality Reappraised: Brain Mechanisms of Transcendent Experience and Beyond

ai.headline: Brain networks linked to transcendent experiences are shared across meditation, psychedelics and epilepsy, not confined to one 'spiritual centre'.
ai.summary: The paper reviews studies of Non-Ordinary Experiences, including meditation, psychedelics, breathwork, hypnosis and neurological events. An fMRI meta-analysis of 34 meditation studies involving 700 people found recruitment of several brain areas rather than a single spiritual centre, and suggests long-term outcomes depend on personal context as well as brain state.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that unusual or transcendent experiences can be understood through brain mechanisms without reducing personal meaning to biology alone.
ai.life_skill: Notice how the setting and your own interpretation shape the meaning of an unusual experience, not just the feeling itself.
ai.fact: A meditation fMRI meta-analysis of 34 studies with 700 participants found aggregate recruitment of the right rolandic operculum, left insula, supplementary motor area and hippocampus.

quiz.question: What did the fMRI meta-analysis of meditation suggest about a 'spiritual centre' in the brain?
quiz.answer: It found recruitment of several brain areas, arguing against a single spiritual centre.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint narrative synthesis, not peer-reviewed, and does not establish causation.

items.title: The role of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in adults with mature T-cell lymphomas.
items.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

ai.headline: A stem cell transplant may not clearly improve survival for adults with rare T-cell lymphomas compared with other transplants.
ai.summary: This Cochrane review looked at allogeneic stem cell transplantation for adults with mature T-cell lymphomas. It found one small trial comparing it with autologous transplantation, suggesting little to no difference in two-year survival, but the evidence was very uncertain.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that for rare blood cancers, strong evidence about whether a risky transplant helps is still lacking.
ai.fact: Mature T-cell lymphomas are rare cancers of immune cells with generally poor outcomes.

quiz.question: What did the review find about allogeneic versus autologous stem cell transplantation for two-year survival?
quiz.answer: It may result in little to no difference, but the evidence is very uncertain.

ai.caveat: The review is based on very few small studies with low to very low certainty evidence and no meta-analysis was possible.

items.title: Genetic diversity must underpin area-based conservation and restoration targets

ai.headline: Conservation targets often ignore genetic diversity, which is vital for species to survive environmental change.
ai.summary: The paper reviews progress on global biodiversity targets and finds that while over 70% of countries have set targets to conserve genetic diversity, only 13% report on the key indicator measuring whether populations are large enough to maintain it. It argues that protecting ecosystems does not automatically protect genetic diversity, and that restoration alone has not been shown to increase genetic diversity.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that saving habitats may not be enough to keep species resilient, which affects the natural systems people rely on.
ai.life_skill: Check whether conservation projects mention genetic diversity and population size, not just the area of land protected.
ai.fact: Genetic diversity underpins ecosystem function and species’ ability to adapt to a changing environment.
ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed and is based on a review of policy progress rather than new experimental data.

items.title: The association between orthorexia nervosa and social media use: A systematic review and meta-analysis

ai.headline: Greater social media use is linked to more orthorexic tendencies, but the link is small and not proven to be causal.
ai.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 33 studies looked at the link between social media use and orthorexia nervosa, an extreme obsession with healthy eating. It found a small positive association between social media use and orthorexic symptoms, and heavier users had greater odds of orthorexia in a secondary analysis.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how we use social media may be connected to unhealthy attitudes about food, though the direction of the link is unclear.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether the food content you see online makes you feel anxious or rigid about eating.
ai.fact: Orthorexia nervosa is described as an extreme obsession with consuming healthy foods that can cause anxiety and impaired functionality.

quiz.question: What did the review find about social media use and orthorexic tendencies?
quiz.answer: It found a small positive association between social media use and orthorexic tendencies.

ai.caveat: All included studies were cross-sectional and the certainty of evidence was very low, so causality and direction cannot be established.

items.title: What the submission does not show: Complexifying cognitive offloading in students' mathematical work with LLMs

ai.headline: A student's final maths answer does not show whether they used an LLM to do the thinking for them.
ai.summary: Researchers tracked 23 first-year university students using LLMs for three linear algebra homework tasks, analysing 429 prompts and 59 chatlogs against submitted work. Students used the LLM as a solver, explainer, or validator, often switching approaches between tasks, and many final answers closely resembled LLM output even after the student had explained, conjectured, and checked their own ideas.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that judging learning from a finished assignment alone can be misleading when AI tools are involved.
ai.life_skill: Notice how you use AI tools—whether you let them solve for you, explain ideas, or check your own thinking—rather than only looking at the final result.
ai.fact: Students in the study shifted between treating an LLM as a solver, explainer, or validator across different homework tasks.

quiz.question: What did the researchers conclude about using a submitted solution as evidence of offloading mathematical work to an LLM?
quiz.answer: An LLM-aided submission is not a trustworthy marker of whether a student offloaded the mathematical work.

ai.caveat: It is a small preprint (not yet peer reviewed) following 23 students, so the findings are not proof and may not apply more widely.

items.title: Multi-agent LLM diagnostic teams improve differential recall on curated cases and reverse on real emergency notes: a label-level reversal without a clinician-judged safety difference

ai.headline: AI diagnostic teams beat single models on curated cases but worse on real emergency notes, with no judged safety difference.
ai.summary: Researchers compared a single AI call, five AI personas in one chat, and five blinded AI agents coordinated by a moderator across curated medical cases and real emergency notes. On curated cases the moderated team improved recall of possible diagnoses but not top accuracy; on real emergency notes it performed worse, though doctors did not judge its errors more dangerous.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that AI tools that look promising in controlled tests may not work the same way in messy real-world settings.
ai.life_skill: Check whether an AI tool was tested on data similar to the situation you want to use it in before trusting its results.
ai.fact: Multi-agent AI pipelines improved differential-list recall on curated medical cases but underperformed on uncurated emergency notes.

quiz.question: What happened when the moderated AI team was tested on real emergency notes compared with curated cases?
quiz.answer: It performed worse on real emergency notes, reversing the improvement seen on curated cases.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: [Perspectives] Wisdom and tenderness

ai.headline: COVID-19 hit young people's mental health hardest, and loneliness was already a widespread problem.
ai.summary: The piece reflects on the mental health toll of the COVID-19 pandemic, noting that children, adolescents, and young adults were worst affected despite lower rates of severe illness. It also highlights loneliness as a pre-existing concern made more visible by pandemic restrictions.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that young people can carry heavy mental health burdens even when they are not physically at high risk from a disease.
ai.life_skill: Notice if you or someone you know feels lonely, and consider reaching out to a trusted person or support service.
ai.fact: Loneliness was a widespread concern before the COVID-19 pandemic.

quiz.question: Which group was hit hardest by the pandemic's mental health toll despite lower rates of severe COVID-19 illness?
quiz.answer: Children, adolescents, and young adults.

ai.caveat: This is a perspective piece, not a study with data, so it reflects the author's views rather than proven findings.

items.title: Olfactory combinatorial coding supports risk–reward decision-making in Caenorhabditis elegans

ai.headline: A worm’s brain weighs attractive and repulsive smells together to decide whether to move toward or away from them.
ai.summary: Researchers imaged the whole nervous system of Caenorhabditis elegans while exposing it to the odorant 1-octanol. They found the smell is encoded at the same time as both an attractant and a repellent, and the brain integrates these opposing signals to set the strength and direction of the worm’s movement response.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how nervous systems can combine conflicting signals to weigh opportunities and hazards when making decisions.
ai.life_skill: Notice when a situation has both good and bad sides before deciding what to do.
ai.fact: The odorant 1-octanol is encoded in C. elegans as both an attractant and a repellent at the same time.

quiz.question: How is 1-octanol encoded in the worm’s periphery?
quiz.answer: It is encoded combinatorially as both an attractant and a repellent.

ai.caveat: The findings come from a single lab study in worms and may not apply to humans.

items.title: Physical exercise and lower psychological distress among rural left-behind adolescents in China: evidence from a moderated serial mediation model

ai.headline: Physical exercise is linked to lower psychological distress in rural left-behind adolescents in China, partly through self-efficacy and emotional intelligence.
ai.summary: A survey of 1,399 rural left-behind adolescent students in China found that physical exercise was significantly linked to lower psychological distress. General self-efficacy and emotional intelligence partly explained this link, with self-efficacy showing the larger indirect association, and the emotional-intelligence pathway was stronger among female students.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests everyday habits like exercise may support teenage mental wellbeing alongside confidence and emotional skills.
ai.life_skill: Try regular physical activity and notice whether it changes how confident you feel and how you handle emotions.
ai.fact: Physical exercise was significantly and negatively correlated with psychological distress among rural left-behind adolescents in China.

quiz.question: What did the study find about physical exercise and psychological distress?
quiz.answer: Physical exercise was significantly linked to lower psychological distress among rural left-behind adolescent students in China.

ai.caveat: This was a cross-sectional survey, so it cannot show that exercise causes lower distress or prove the order in which these factors influence each other.

items.title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models

ai.headline: AI models learn to write “wait” from training data, not just from reinforcement learning.
ai.summary: The study traced how the word “wait” appears in AI reasoning models. It found that reinforcement learning rarely invents the word from scratch; instead, models usually inherit it from their training data or fine-tuning, and RL often just increases how often it is used.
ai.why_it_matters: This helps people understand that AI “reasoning” behaviours can come from copied patterns in data rather than genuine new thinking.
ai.life_skill: Notice when an AI pauses or says “wait” and treat it as a copied pattern, not proof of careful reasoning.
ai.fact: Large reinforcement-learning accuracy gains can happen without the word “wait” appearing in model outputs.

quiz.question: Does reinforcement learning usually create the word “wait” in models that never used it before?
quiz.answer: No, zero-RL almost never coins the marker; it usually arrives with training data or fine-tuning.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and is based on sampled outputs from open models rather than a general proof about all AI systems.

items.title: Combining Dispositional and Behavioural Facets of SRL, and the Role of Students' Growth Orientation

ai.headline: Combining self-reported and logged study habits gives a fuller picture of how students regulate their learning.
ai.summary: Researchers looked at 5,724 business students, comparing their own reports of self-regulated learning with computer-logged behaviour. They found high-performing students flexibly switch between deep and surface learning depending on context, and that growth orientation—mindsets, effort beliefs, future goals and autonomous motivation—links to both regulation styles and course performance.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that mixing how students say they study with what they actually do online can help target useful feedback for learners.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether you switch between deep and surface study depending on the task, rather than sticking to one approach.
ai.fact: High-performing students flexibly switch between deep and surface learning modes based on context.

quiz.question: What did the study find about high-performing students and learning approaches?
quiz.answer: High-performing students flexibly switch between deep and surface learning modes based on context.

ai.caveat: The findings come from one observational study of business students, so they show links rather than prove cause and effect and may not apply to other groups.

items.title: Extreme weather events: A practical guide for clinicians
authors: Courtney Howard, Enrique Barros, William Gagnon, Calae Philippe, Poornima Prabhakaran, Cecilia Sorensen

ai.headline: Clinicians should plan for extreme weather to protect patients and keep care running during disasters.
ai.summary: This is a practical guide for clinicians on managing extreme weather events. It recommends assessing patient exposure and vulnerability, creating emergency plans and kits, maintaining continuity of care during disasters, prioritising high-acuity patients and essential treatments, and checking on missed medications and mental health impacts afterwards.
ai.why_it_matters: Extreme weather can disrupt healthcare and endanger vulnerable people, so knowing how to prepare helps protect health in everyday life.
ai.life_skill: Try making a simple emergency plan and kit with any essential medicines or devices you might need if severe weather strikes.
ai.fact: Extreme weather events can disrupt access to essential treatments such as insulin, dialysis, and oxygen.

quiz.question: What should clinicians do after a disaster regarding patients?
quiz.answer: Ask patients about missed doses of drugs, missed appointments, and mental health impacts.

ai.caveat: This is a practical guide based on expert opinion rather than a research study with measured results.

items.title: Research on Optimizing the Use of Technology With Education

ai.headline: A trial will test whether a behavioural programme helps adolescents with type 1 diabetes use glucose monitors more consistently.
ai.summary: The study focuses on young adolescents with type 1 diabetes who are less likely to start or keep using continuous glucose monitors. It will test a behavioural intervention designed to improve CGM use, especially among underrepresented groups in diabetes technology research.
ai.why_it_matters: Better use of glucose monitors is linked to improved blood sugar control and health outcomes for young people with type 1 diabetes.
ai.life_skill: Talk to your diabetes care team about support options if you find it hard to keep using a glucose monitor.
ai.fact: Consistent use of continuous glucose monitors has the potential to improve glycemic control and related type 1 diabetes health outcomes.

quiz.question: What is the trial testing in adolescents with type 1 diabetes?
quiz.answer: It is testing a behavioural intervention designed to optimise use of continuous glucose monitors.

ai.caveat: This is a feasibility trial with results posted on a clinical trial register, not yet peer-reviewed published evidence.

items.title: Glymphatic System Is Enhanced in Anti-NMDAR Encephalitis and Facilitates Antibody Influx and Clearance in the Brain

ai.headline: In a mouse model, brain waste-clearance channels opened up, letting disease-causing antibodies in and out faster.
ai.summary: Researchers studied mice with a specific type of brain inflammation to see how the brain's cleaning system, called the glymphatic system, behaves. They found that this system became more active, which helped remove waste but also allowed harmful antibodies to enter the brain more easily.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that the brain's internal plumbing can sometimes work against us by letting in the very things that cause disease, not just removing waste.
ai.fact: The glymphatic system uses a protein called aquaporin-4 to move fluid in and out of the brain tissue.

quiz.question: Did the increased activity of the cleaning system help or hurt the mice in this study?
quiz.answer: It had mixed effects: it helped clear antibodies but also allowed more of them to enter the brain, causing injury.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint (not yet peer reviewed) based on mouse models, so results may not apply to humans.

items.title: Millions take fish oil for brain health. A two-year study found no benefit

ai.headline: A two-year trial found fish oil supplements did not improve memory or protect against brain shrinkage.
ai.summary: Researchers conducted a two-year clinical trial to see if fish oil supplements could benefit brain health. While the supplements successfully delivered omega-3s to the brain, they failed to improve memory or prevent Alzheimer's-related brain shrinkage.
ai.why_it_matters: This suggests that relying on pills for brain health may be ineffective, and that getting nutrients through a balanced diet might be more beneficial.
ai.life_skill: Consider whether your overall diet provides the nutrients you need rather than relying solely on supplements.
ai.fact: Fish oil supplements can deliver omega-3s to the brain without necessarily improving memory or preventing brain shrinkage.

quiz.question: Did the fish oil supplements in the study improve participants' memory?
quiz.answer: No, the study found that the supplements failed to improve memory.

ai.caveat: This is a news report summarising a single clinical trial, so the results may not apply to everyone or all types of brain health issues.

items.title: Daily Briefing: Tiny doses of LSD seem to boost cognition

ai.headline: Tiny doses of LSD may improve focus, but only in women, according to a brief news report.
ai.summary: A Nature news briefing reports on research into tiny doses of LSD and cognition. It says the drug improved the ability to focus, but only in women. The briefing does not give details of the study’s size or design.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that a substance’s effects on focus may differ between men and women, highlighting why research should check both sexes.
ai.fact: Tiny doses of LSD are linked to improved focus in women, according to a Nature news briefing.

quiz.question: Who did the reported LSD research find had improved focus?
quiz.answer: The briefing says the improvement was seen only in women.

ai.caveat: This is a short news briefing, not a full study, so it gives no details about participants, methods, or whether the result is reliable.

items.title: Determinants of response to CAR T cell therapy in a multicenter, multi-trial cohort analysis of patients with lymphoma

ai.headline: Certain T cells in CAR T therapy products are linked to better and longer-lasting benefit for lymphoma patients.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed samples from clinical trials of people with non-Hodgkin lymphoma who received anti-CD19 CAR T cell therapy. They found that products containing more naive-like and stem cell memory-like T cells were linked to improved and prolonged clinical benefit, a result confirmed in a separate group using different products.
ai.why_it_matters: This helps scientists understand why some cancer immunotherapies work better than others and could guide future treatment development.
ai.fact: In CAR T cell therapy for lymphoma, the type of T cells in the treatment product is linked to how well and how long the treatment works.

quiz.question: What feature of the CAR T product was linked to better outcomes in lymphoma patients?
quiz.answer: A high proportion of naive-like and stem cell memory-like CCR7+CD45RA+ T cells was linked to improved and prolonged clinical benefit.

ai.caveat: The study shows a link rather than proving that the T cells cause the better outcomes, and it focused on people with lymphoma receiving CAR T therapy.

items.title: Your brain maps out numbers, including integers and fractions

ai.headline: Brain scans show a map of activity for whole numbers and fractions in adults.
ai.summary: Researchers took dynamic brain scans of adults presented with integers and fractions. The scans revealed a map of brain activity that underlies how we arrange numerical information. The findings were published in PLOS Biology.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how the brain handles the numbers used in everyday calculations.
ai.fact: Brain activity can be mapped to show how the brain organises whole numbers and fractions.

quiz.question: What did the brain scans reveal about integers and fractions?
quiz.answer: They revealed a map of brain activity underlying how we arrange numerical information, including integers and fractions.

ai.caveat: The summary is from a news report of a single study, so details such as sample size and exact methods are not available.

items.title: New test measures potentially harmful metals in cellulose food packaging

ai.headline: New test detects potentially harmful metals in cellulose food packaging.
ai.summary: A paper discusses a new technique for detecting potentially harmful metals in regenerated cellulose food packaging. The tool is intended for safety assessments of packaging materials increasingly used as alternatives to conventional plastics.
ai.why_it_matters: It means packaging used instead of plastic can be checked for metals that might be harmful.
ai.life_skill: Check what material your food packaging is made from.

ai.headline: A multi-model adversarial checking system can catch LLM errors that standard checks miss, with an auditable record trail.
ai.summary: The paper studies LLM-generated records that can be both correct and wrong at the same time, such as a true fact next to a hallucination. BiasGuard-D uses two adversarial AI roles from different model families, a three-model quorum vote, and combined referential-plus-semantic checks to detect defects; on HaluEval QA it raised right-answer recovery by 49 percentage points.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI outputs might be checked more reliably and transparently as they become part of everyday information systems.
ai.life_skill: Check important AI-generated information against a second source before relying on it.
ai.fact: A single LLM-generated record can simultaneously contain a grounded fact and a hallucination.

quiz.question: What did BiasGuard-D add to catch errors that referential checks miss?
quiz.answer: It added a semantic component that fires on verdicts referential checks miss.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and the results come from a proposed system evaluated on a specific QA benchmark rather than independent real-world trials.

items.title: RealMe: Immersive Volumetric Video from Minimal Captures

ai.headline: AI enhances low-resolution videos
ai.summary: Researchers studied creating immersive volumetric videos from sparse captures. They proposed a framework called RealMe, which enhances limited captures into high-resolution videos. RealMe outperforms state-of-the-art methods in visual fidelity and consistency.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because it could improve video production and consumption in everyday life and various industries.
ai.life_skill: Try exploring AI video editing tools to enhance your own videos.
ai.fact: RealMe is a unified framework that enhances low-resolution videos into high-resolution, 4D-consistent videos.

quiz.question: What is the name of the proposed framework?
quiz.answer: The proposed framework is called RealMe.

items.title: Developmental trajectories organize the assembly of valence circuits in the central amygdala

ai.headline: Developmental trajectories shape amygdala circuits
ai.summary: Researchers studied how neural circuits in the central amygdala develop. They found that developmental trajectories organize the assembly of valence-specific circuits. These trajectories give rise to future appetitive and aversive neurons.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how neural circuits develop can help explain how emotions and behaviors are formed
ai.life_skill: Notice how your emotions and behaviors develop over time
ai.fact: The central amygdala contains distinct neural circuits for appetitive and aversive behaviors

quiz.question: What part of the brain do the researchers study?
quiz.answer: The central amygdala

items.title: The CTF is dead, long live the CTF? Exploring perspectives on AI and the recognition of skill in capture-the-flag competitions

ai.headline: AI is changing how capture-the-flag competitions signal skill and how security learners are judged.
ai.summary: This exploratory qualitative study interviewed seven experienced CTF organisers and players and received eleven anonymous written responses. Participants disagreed about AI’s role, with some criticising AI-assisted solving, others wanting AI built into competitions, and many noting that rankings now reflect access to AI and money, while some students solved challenges without being able to explain how.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how automation can weaken the value of a skill measure and force communities to rethink what counts as genuine ability.
ai.life_skill: Try explaining how you solved a problem, not just getting the right answer.
ai.fact: Capture-the-flag competitions are used to recruit talent, build skills and sustain a competitive culture in the security community.

quiz.question: What did some participants say about students who solved CTF challenges quickly with AI?
quiz.answer: They could solve challenges quickly but could not explain how they had done so.

items.title: Comparing the Impact of Augmented Reality and Electronic Popular Science Picture Books on Vocabulary and Reading in Preschool Children

ai.headline: Electronic picture books helped preschoolers learn science words better, while augmented reality books boosted motivation and deeper understanding.
ai.summary: Sixty-two children aged 5-6 were randomly assigned to read popular science picture books either as augmented reality books or electronic books over two weeks. The electronic group scored higher on target vocabulary, explicit reading comprehension and physical engagement, while the augmented reality group showed stronger implicit reading comprehension, intrinsic motivation, verbal engagement and emotional engagement.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that different digital reading formats can support different kinds of learning, so choosing the right format may depend on whether the goal is learning facts or building motivation and deeper understanding.
ai.life_skill: Try matching the reading format to your goal: use simple electronic books for learning new words and facts, and more interactive formats to spark curiosity and deeper thinking.
ai.fact: Physical and verbal engagement helped explain how multimedia reading media influenced reading comprehension in this study.
ai.caveat: The study involved only 62 children aged 5-6 over two weeks, so the results may not apply to older children, longer periods, or other subjects.

items.title: Enzyme-embedded polyesters for accelerated biodegradation in the deep sea

ai.headline: Enzyme-embedded compostable plastics break down almost completely in the deep sea while keeping their strength.
ai.summary: The study tested compostable polyesters with enzymes embedded using heat. These materials degraded nearly completely in deep-sea conditions and across marine environments without losing their performance.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a possible way to reduce long-lasting plastic pollution in oceans while still using durable materials.
ai.life_skill: Check whether plastic items are labelled compostable before choosing them.
ai.fact: Thermal enzyme embedding can greatly speed up the breakdown of compostable polyesters in marine environments.

quiz.question: What happened to the enzyme-embedded compostable polyesters in the deep sea?
quiz.answer: They showed near-complete degradation while preserving material performance.

ai.caveat: This is a single materials study, so real-world results may vary and it does not prove all enzyme-embedded plastics will behave the same way.

items.title: Conflict and climate change are driving food shortages

ai.headline: Conflict and climate change drive food shortages
ai.summary: Researchers studied global food security and found that conflict and climate change are driving localised food shortages. Despite increased global calorie production, conflict affects food production, access, and affordability. The Food and Agriculture Organization identified 13 countries with expected increases in acute food insecurity.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because food shortages have long-term negative impacts on health, particularly in areas affected by conflict and climate change.
ai.life_skill: Check how your daily food choices might impact global food security.
ai.fact: Conflict and climate change are linked to food shortages worldwide.

quiz.question: What are the main drivers of localised food shortages?
quiz.answer: Conflict and climate change are the main drivers of localised food shortages.

ai.caveat: This study is based on a report and may not be a comprehensive or peer-reviewed analysis of the issue.

items.title: Study finds air quality warnings had only a modest impact on Montrealers' movements during wildfires

ai.headline: Air quality warnings during wildfires changed Montrealers' travel only modestly.
ai.summary: The study looked at Montrealers' travel patterns during Canada's worst wildfire smoke episodes when Environment and Climate Change Canada urged people to limit outdoor activity. Movement did change, but far less than public health officials might have hoped.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that warnings alone may not be enough to change how people behave during smoky wildfire conditions.
ai.life_skill: Check local air quality alerts and consider reducing outdoor activity when smoke levels are high.
ai.fact: Public health warnings during wildfire smoke episodes led to only modest changes in travel patterns in Montreal.

quiz.question: How much did air quality warnings affect Montrealers' movements during wildfires?
quiz.answer: They had only a modest impact on travel patterns.

ai.caveat: The findings are based on observed travel patterns during specific wildfire episodes and cannot prove the warnings caused the changes.

items.title: Novel but stable endosymbionts have contrasting effects on aphid dispersal and plant feeding damage in the cereal pest Diuraphis noxia

ai.headline: Certain bacteria inside aphids can change how much crop damage they cause and whether they spread.
ai.summary: Researchers put two types of bacteria into Russian wheat aphids, a cereal pest. One bacterium made feeding damage and aphid numbers worse, while the other reduced both; the first also stopped aphids from growing wings and dispersing.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how tiny organisms living inside insects can influence crop damage and pest spread, which matters for food production.
ai.fact: Endosymbiotic bacteria can alter aphid feeding damage on wheat and barley and affect whether aphids develop wings and disperse.

quiz.question: What did the two bacteria do differently to aphid feeding damage?
quiz.answer: Rickettsiella increased feeding damage while Regiella reduced it.

ai.caveat: This is a single controlled experiment in one aphid species, so the results may not apply to other pests or field conditions.

items.title: Use green transition funds to achieve health for all, suggest experts

ai.headline: Experts say green energy transition funds could help pay for universal health coverage in poorer countries.
ai.summary: The article reports expert opinion in The BMJ's climate issue that money from the green energy transition could be used to finance universal health coverage in low- and middle-income countries.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how climate spending might also improve health and reduce inequality around the world.
ai.life_skill: Notice how money spent on one problem, such as climate change, can sometimes help solve another, such as access to healthcare.
ai.fact: Universal health coverage means everyone can get the health services they need without financial hardship.

quiz.question: What do experts suggest green transition funds could help achieve in low- and middle-income countries?
quiz.answer: They suggest the funds could help finance universal health coverage.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about expert opinion, not a research study with data or proof.

items.title: Scientists discover ghostly, eyeless creature hidden in Chinese cave

ai.headline: Scientists found a rare, eyeless cave snail in China, with only three living adults seen.
ai.summary: Researchers explored a high-altitude cave in China and discovered a ghostly, eyeless freshwater snail adapted to live entirely in darkness. It is the first recorded discovery of its kind in China, and only three living adults were found.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how little we still know about hidden underground life and how quickly rare species can be at risk.

quiz.question: How many living adults of the new snail species did researchers find?
quiz.answer: Researchers found only three living adults.

items.title: Electronic Quitline Referral With Enhanced Academic Detailing for the Promotion of Smoking Cessation

ai.headline: Quitline eReferral aids smoking cessation
ai.summary: This phase IV clinical trial studied the impact of an electronic Quitline referral system on smoking cessation. The system was implemented with an enhanced academic detailing strategy in community health centers. The trial examined the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of this approach.
ai.why_it_matters: This research matters because it could help increase tobacco cessation treatment among disadvantaged patients who use tobacco.
ai.life_skill: Try seeking help from a Quitline if you want to stop smoking.
ai.fact: Smoking is linked to tobacco-related carcinoma.

quiz.question: What was the main goal of this clinical trial?
quiz.answer: To determine the impact of an electronic Quitline referral system on Quitline reach and self-reported quit rates.

items.title: Future in mind: Systematic review of compassion-based interventions in higher education and feasibility study of Compassionate Mind Training with pre-registration Mental Health Student Nurses
items.venue: Edinburgh Napier Research Repository (Edinburgh Napier University)

ai.headline: Compassion-based training may be acceptable and feasible for student nurses, but more trials are needed.
ai.summary: A review of 33 studies involving 4,897 higher education students looked at how compassion-based interventions are recruited and delivered. A separate small feasibility study of Compassionate Mind Training with 38 first-year mental health student nurses found high acceptability and positive wellbeing measure responses, though it was not a randomised trial.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how student wellbeing support might be tested and improved in demanding courses like nursing.
ai.life_skill: Try noticing when you are self-critical and respond to yourself with the same kindness you would offer a friend.
ai.fact: Compassion-based interventions are being studied as ways to prevent and address psychological problems in higher education students.

quiz.question: What did the feasibility study find about Compassionate Mind Training for student nurses?
quiz.answer: Participants rated it highly on enjoyableness, usefulness and clarity, and qualitative feedback indicated it was acceptable.

items.title: Effects of dance-based physical activity on cognitive and psychological health across age groups: a systematic review.

ai.headline: Dance-based activity may help some thinking and mood outcomes, especially in older adults, but evidence is mixed.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 22 controlled trials with 1,645 people aged 4 to 94 looked at dance-based physical activity. It found some favourable links with global cognition, memory, attention, depression, anxiety, stress, well-being and quality of life, but results were inconsistent and executive function findings were mixed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows dance could be a low-cost way to support mental and cognitive health, though stronger evidence is still needed.
ai.life_skill: Try joining a regular dance or movement class to see if it helps your mood and focus.
ai.fact: Dance-based physical activity combines motor, cognitive, emotional and social elements.

quiz.answer: Findings for executive function were mixed.

ai.caveat: Many studies had a high risk of bias, samples were small, and most evidence came from older adults, so firm conclusions cannot be drawn.

items.title: Effects of Active Video Games on Cardiometabolic Health in Children and Adolescents: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

ai.headline: Active video games may slightly lower BMI and blood pressure in children and teens.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 14 randomised trials with 942 children and adolescents aged 4-18. Active video games were linked to small reductions in body mass index and systolic blood pressure, while effects on other heart and metabolism measures were uncertain.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that active video games can be a fun way to add movement and may support heart health in young people.
ai.life_skill: Try swapping some seated screen time for active video games that get you moving.
ai.fact: Active video games were associated with small reductions in BMI and systolic blood pressure in children and adolescents.

quiz.question: What did active video games reduce in children and adolescents according to the review?
quiz.answer: They were associated with small reductions in BMI and systolic blood pressure.

ai.caveat: The evidence is based on a limited number of trials and certainty for many outcomes remains uncertain.

items.title: The Role of Community Pharmacists in Identifying and Managing Insomnia and Facilitating Access to Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) – a Systematic Review

ai.headline: Community pharmacists may help identify insomnia and guide people toward CBT-I, but this is not yet common practice.
ai.summary: A systematic review of nine studies looked at how community pharmacists manage chronic insomnia. It found pharmacists could spot insomnia during counselling, reduce inappropriate sleeping medicines, and signpost or deliver CBT-I, though standard protocols, referral routes and time are lacking.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a possible way to get evidence-based sleep help more easily through a local pharmacy rather than only a GP or specialist.
ai.life_skill: If you struggle with sleep, ask your community pharmacist whether they can screen for insomnia or point you to CBT-I.
ai.fact: Insomnia affects approximately 10% of the global adult population.

quiz.question: What did the review find about community pharmacists and insomnia?
quiz.answer: They could identify insomnia, deprescribe inappropriate hypnotics, and in some settings deliver or signpost patients to CBT-I.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the included studies were limited by a lack of standardised protocols, referral pathways and time constraints.

items.title: Family Educational and Cultural Practices Amplify Rather than Buffer Socioeconomic Inequalities in Academic Achievement in France

ai.headline: Family educational practices may widen, not narrow, school achievement gaps linked to family background in France.
ai.summary: Researchers followed 12,904 French students from Grade 5 to Grade 9 and looked at family background and home educational practices such as cultural activities and parental involvement. Practices were linked to higher achievement overall, but when they made a difference they tended to help students from higher-background families more, reinforcing rather than reducing gaps.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that extra home support does not automatically close achievement gaps and can sometimes make them wider.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether the extra educational activities you do at home are helping everyone equally or mainly those who already have advantages.
ai.fact: In this French study, family educational practices were generally more beneficial for students from higher socioeconomic backgrounds.

quiz.question: Did family educational practices mainly reduce or reinforce socioeconomic achievement gaps in this study?
quiz.answer: They tended to reinforce gaps by being more beneficial for students from higher socioeconomic backgrounds.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and as an observational study it cannot prove that family practices cause the achievement patterns.

items.title: Engagement or disengagement: understanding the emotional dynamics of EFL learners in GenAI-assisted writing from the sociocultural perspective

ai.headline: Students' feelings about using AI for English writing change over time and differ from person to person.
ai.summary: Researchers followed three Chinese university students learning English as a foreign language over a 14-week course that used generative AI for writing tasks. They found three different emotional patterns: one student stayed mostly positive, one moved from practical disengagement to critical engagement, and one moved from moderate disengagement to a breakdown and stronger disengagement. These patterns were shaped by a mix of personal factors, such as English proficiency and AI literacy, and environmental factors, such as task design and teacher or peer support.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that AI tools do not affect every learner's emotions in the same way, so support needs to be tailored to individual students.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your own feelings change when you use AI for schoolwork and ask a teacher or peer for help if you become discouraged.
ai.fact: Emotional engagement with AI-assisted writing is a dynamic and fluid state that interacts with behavioural and cognitive engagement over time.

quiz.question: What did the study find about students' emotional engagement with GenAI-assisted writing?
quiz.answer: It found three distinct trajectories—positive-resilient, pragmatic-transformative, and vulnerable-contingent—shaped by individual and environmental factors.

ai.caveat: The findings come from only three students in one course, so they may not apply to all learners or settings.

items.title: PI-MLLM: Psychophysics-Inspired Multimodal Large Language Model for Oddly Satisfying Video Emotion Analysis

ai.headline: A new AI model uses physical sensory cues to better predict emotions from oddly satisfying videos.
ai.summary: Researchers built a dataset of 12,000 short oddly satisfying videos labelled for viewer emotion under video-only, audio-only and audio-visual conditions. They then created PI-MLLM, an AI model that aligns visual motion and sound cues and uses Shapley attribution to show which sense drives the emotion. Tests suggest it improves emotion prediction and sensory-grounded explanations.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how sight and sound together shape feelings from everyday online videos, helping us understand digital media effects.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether a video’s feeling comes from what you see, what you hear, or both together.
ai.fact: Oddly satisfying videos can evoke strong responses through repetitive motion, visual tactility and ASMR-like sounds despite few explicit emotion cues.

quiz.question: What does PI-MLLM use Shapley attribution for?
quiz.answer: To identify the dominant modality and determine whether visual and auditory evidence is synergistic or conflicting.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and the findings come from experiments on a newly constructed dataset rather than independent confirmation.

items.title: Examining the roles of socioeconomic status and relevant health correlates (body mass index, diet quality, and inflammation) for neuropsychological function in young adults

ai.headline: Higher body mass index and more sugar or fat in the diet are linked to lower cognitive performance in young adults.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 109 young adults to see whether body mass index, inflammation, or diet explained the link between socioeconomic status and thinking skills. Body mass index did not explain that link, but higher body mass index and higher sugar and fat intake were linked to lower cognitive scores. Sugar intake appeared to partly link body mass index to cognition, but this disappeared after adjusting for other factors.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that everyday eating habits and body weight may be connected to how well young adults think, even if the exact causes are still unclear.
ai.life_skill: Notice how different foods and meals affect your energy and concentration, and consider eating more balanced meals.
ai.fact: Higher body mass index and higher sugar and fat intake were inversely correlated with cognitive functioning in this sample of young adults.

quiz.question: Did body mass index explain the link between socioeconomic status and cognition?
quiz.answer: No, BMI did not account for the association between SES and cognition.

ai.caveat: This was a small cross-sectional study of 109 young adults, so it cannot show cause and effect.

items.title: A Mechanistic Theory Unifying Value and Schema in the Prefrontal Cortex

ai.headline: A new brain model suggests value signals control how we use learned context to make flexible choices.
ai.summary: The paper studies how the prefrontal cortex handles both value and world structure. It proposes that value acts as a control signal gating structured working memory of the current context to guide behaviour, rather than simply reading out actions. Recurrent neural networks trained with reinforcement or supervised learning reproduced this model across value-based tasks.
ai.why_it_matters: It offers a fresh way to understand how people adapt decisions in new situations using what they already know about the world.
ai.life_skill: Notice when a familiar pattern helps you make a quick choice in a new situation.
ai.fact: The prefrontal cortex is involved in both computing value and learning the structure of the world.

quiz.question: In the proposed model, what role does value play in behaviour?
quiz.answer: Value acts as a control signal that gates structured working memory of the current context to control behaviour.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and based on computational models rather than direct human evidence.

items.title: Transparency, accountability, and scholarly integrity: A systematic narrative review of artificial intelligence governance frameworks in healthcare publication

ai.headline: Guidance on using AI in healthcare publishing has grown but remains fragmented and uneven in authority.
ai.summary: The review examined 100 publications on how AI should be reported and governed in healthcare research, including 69 guidelines, frameworks and policies. It found guidance has shifted from focusing on AI model performance to wider issues such as fairness, transparency, human oversight and generative AI, but the landscape remains fragmented with varying levels of authority.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how scientific research involving AI is being steered, which affects the reliability of health information people may encounter.
ai.life_skill: Check whether health research you read discloses how AI was used and follow guidance from qualified professionals for health decisions.
ai.fact: Guidance on AI in healthcare publications has evolved from model performance transparency toward broader sociotechnical accountability between 2018 and 2026.

quiz.question: What did the review find about AI governance in healthcare publications?
quiz.answer: It found the guidance has evolved toward broader accountability but remains fragmented and uneven in authority.

ai.caveat: This is a single systematic narrative review, so its synthesis reflects the included sources and search window rather than definitive proof.

items.title: Submission Timing in Take-Home Exams, Procrastination Perceptions, and Their Impact on Grades
items.venue: Journal of Further and Higher Education

ai.headline: Submitting take-home exams neither too early nor too late may be linked to better grades.
ai.summary: Researchers studied fourth-year college students taking take-home exams, looking at submission timing and survey responses about procrastination. Moderate delays in submitting were linked to higher scores, while excessive delays were linked to lower performance. Procrastination was commonly linked to feeling overwhelmed, lack of motivation, fear of failure, and perfectionism, and was associated with higher stress.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that timing of work can be linked to results, and that leaving things too long may increase stress and hurt goals.
ai.life_skill: Notice when you are delaying starting work and check whether you feel overwhelmed or afraid of failing.
ai.fact: Procrastination is commonly linked to higher stress and negative effects on personal and professional goals.

quiz.question: What was linked to higher exam scores in the study?
quiz.answer: Moderate submission delays were correlated with higher scores.

ai.caveat: The study shows links between submission timing and grades, not that timing caused the results.

items.title: ElderTree Via a Voice Activated Device for Managing Chronic Health Conditions (NHLBI)

ai.headline: A trial will test whether voice-activated devices help older adults manage multiple chronic conditions better than typing-based systems.
ai.summary: The study compares a voice-based version of the ElderTree health platform with a text/typing-based version for older adults with multiple chronic conditions. quiz.question: What is the study comparing?
quiz.answer: It is comparing a voice-based platform with a text/typing-based platform for delivering the ElderTree health intervention to older adults with multiple chronic conditions.

items.title: “Postcode lottery” for children in England accessing healthcare, report warns

items.title: How a walk in the woods can be good for mental health

ai.headline: Nature sounds, biodiversity awareness and educational signs may improve mood during woodland walks.
ai.summary: Researchers at the University of New Hampshire looked at what makes a walk in the woods boost mood. They found that nature sounds, people’s awareness of biodiversity and educational signage about animals, birds and trees all appear to play a role.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests simple features of green spaces could support everyday mental wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Try noticing the sounds and variety of plants and animals on your next walk in a wood or park.
ai.fact: Spending time in nature is linked to better mood.

quiz.question: What did University of New Hampshire research link to mood-boosting woodland walks?
quiz.answer: Nature sounds, awareness of biodiversity and educational signage about animals, birds and trees.

items.title: Label-free, low-cost AI ranking for systematic review screening

ai.headline: A low-cost AI tool can rank research papers for systematic reviews accurately and cheaply.
ai.summary: The study tested Jev, an AI model that scores research records against eligibility criteria without needing training labels. Across 128 reviews and nearly 170,000 records, Jev outperformed the best free ranker and matched a much more expensive AI at a tiny fraction of the cost, though safely stopping screening still required human decisions.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI can make reviewing research evidence faster and cheaper, which matters because systematic reviews help shape reliable health guidance.
ai.life_skill: Check whether a research summary says how studies were selected and whether human reviewers made the final decisions.
ai.fact: Jev reached at least 95% recall in all 51 Cochrane reviews when ranking was combined with statistical stopping, while reading only 86-88% of records.

quiz.question: What did Jev need to reach 95% recall in all 51 Cochrane reviews?
quiz.answer: Jev ranking combined with statistical stopping reached 95% recall in all 51 reviews, while a fixed score threshold did not.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and safely stopping screening still required human screening decisions.

items.title: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable

ai.headline: The ageing brain may shift from remembering details to understanding the bigger picture.
ai.summary: Researchers propose that ageing changes the brain’s focus from detailed memory to grasping the wider picture. This shift may be an evolutionary adaptation that supports wisdom and passing knowledge to younger generations.
ai.why_it_matters: It reframes normal ageing as a potentially useful change rather than simple decline.
ai.life_skill: Notice what you understand about the big picture rather than only what details you forget.
ai.fact: Ageing may shift brain focus from remembering details to understanding the bigger picture.

quiz.question: What does the research suggest the ageing brain may shift its focus from?
quiz.answer: From remembering details to understanding the bigger picture.

ai.caveat: This is a news report of a proposed idea, not evidence from a study.

items.title: Transparent minispheres reveal that some look-alike cancer drugs part ways in 3D

ai.headline: Two cancer drugs that looked identical in flat lab tests behaved differently in 3D cell clusters.
ai.summary: Researchers adapted an imaging technique to observe individual cells within small 3D groups of cancer cells. They found that two drugs, which appeared to have the same effect in standard flat cultures, actually worked differently in the 3D environment. This difference was linked to how each drug activated the cell's p53 stress response.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that simple lab tests can miss important differences in how medicines work, which is crucial for developing effective treatments.
ai.fact: Standard flat cell cultures may not accurately predict how drugs behave in more complex 3D biological structures.

quiz.question: Why did the two drugs appear different in the 3D test but not the flat test?
quiz.answer: The 3D environment revealed differences in how each drug switched on the cell's p53 stress response.

ai.caveat: This is a preliminary lab study using cell clusters, not a clinical trial in humans, so it does not prove these drugs will behave this way in patients.

items.title: Unsupervised Tool Evolution for Coding Agents in Data-Lake Analytics

ai.headline: AI coding agents can build reusable tools to solve data problems faster without needing expert labels.
ai.summary: Researchers developed a system called TEAL that allows AI agents to create and refine reusable tools for analysing data lakes. By using synthetic questions and feedback from the agent's own attempts, the system improved performance on benchmark tests, especially when the agent had a limited number of steps to solve a problem.

items.title: An integrated human forebrain organoid reveals microglia-mediated CD8 + T cell recruitment and neuroimmune dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease pathology

ai.headline: Lab-grown human brain tissue shows immune cells may drive Alzheimer’s inflammation through a feedback loop.
ai.summary: Researchers built a human brain organoid containing microglia and CD8+ T cells to model Alzheimer’s disease. They found microglia clear amyloid-β and support neurons but also trigger inflammation and recruit T cells via CCL4/5 signaling, creating a neuroinflammatory loop. Blocking CCR5 or CXCR3 reduced T cell recruitment and affected autophagy in microglia.
ai.why_it_matters: It reveals a possible immune mechanism behind Alzheimer’s brain inflammation and offers a human-relevant way to test future treatments.
ai.fact: Microglia can both clear amyloid-β and recruit CD8+ T cells through CCL4/5 signaling via CCR1/5 and CXCR3 in this human brain organoid model.

quiz.question: What did blocking CCR5 or CXCR3 do in the organoid model?
quiz.answer: It blocked CD8+ T cell recruitment and modulated autophagy in a microglia-dependent manner.

ai.caveat: This is early laboratory research using human brain organoids, not people with Alzheimer’s, so it does not prove what happens in real patients.

items.title: Credit Markets with New Screening Technologies -- by Maryam Farboodi, Péter Kondor, Pablo Kurlat

ai.headline: Similar AI screening tools can split credit markets into separate segments with different interest rates.
ai.summary: The authors use an economic model to study how lenders screen borrowers and set interest rates. They find that when lenders make independent screening errors, one market segment forms with smoothly rising rates. When screening errors are correlated, such as from similar AI systems or shared data, lenders specialise into distinct segments, creating a hockey-stick interest-rate schedule where some segments have uniform rates but mixed borrower quality, while others have uniform borrower quality but varied rates.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how new AI and data-sharing tools in banking can change who gets credit and at what price, potentially helping or harming people who are financially excluded.
ai.life_skill: Check how different lenders assess applications before applying for credit, since similar screening systems may produce similar outcomes.
ai.fact: Rejected borrowers reapplying elsewhere can create a pool externality that affects competitors’ applicant pools.

quiz.question: What happens to credit-market segments when lenders’ screening errors are correlated rather than independent?
quiz.answer: Lenders specialise into qualitatively distinct segments, producing a hockey-stick interest-rate schedule with uniform rates in some segments and dispersed rates in others.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and is based on a theoretical model rather than real-world data.
